results.content: What Is The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007994 Overview All directory websites generate leads from visitors who contact professional members. This add-on allows the site to instantly send leads to members without manually matching them. This means members will automatically be connected with leads and have the ability to purchase them in real-time. The website will generate more revenue from leads than ever before! How To Get This Add-On Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available: Join The VIP Add-Ons Club Purchase Individually: Automatic Lead Matching Add-On How It Works This add-on enhances the default Leads system included with all sites by introducing advanced settings and automated matching tools that help speed up lead processing. By default, leads submitted through the "Get Matched" form are marked as Pending and require manual review by an admin—a task that can become overwhelming when submissions start piling up. How to Match a Lead » Get Matched Form With the auto-matching feature enabled, the system can automatically match leads based on the request details, saving time and reducing the need for hands-on management. It’s important to note that auto-matching only applies to leads submitted through the "Get Matched" form—typically found at /getmatched—and only if the visitor requests replies from multiple members. Leads sent directly to a specific member are not auto-matched, though they can still be auto-delivered using a separate setting. Enable "Get Replies from more members?" Option This feature is ideal for websites receiving a high volume of leads and looking to reduce manual work. For new or low-volume sites, we generally recommend sticking with the default leads system until there's a need for more automation. Review the entire documentation folder for more information: >> Automatic Lead Matching Add-On Folder Additional Settings This add-on introduces three additional options to the Leads Settings dropdown, giving more control over how leads are handled. General Settings Each additional option is explained in the following section: Lead Settings » General Settings Auto-Match & Create New Workflow Each setting is explained in the following section: Default Lead Action & Creating New Lead Actions For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Benefits & Limitations Of The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Benefits & Limitations Of The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007995 The following documentation is exclusively for the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". To purchase the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". >> Automatic Lead Matching Benefits Of Auto-Matching More time Eliminate the need to manually match leads to additional members. Set the maximum number of leads that can be sent for every lead entry For example, set it so that up to 10 members can be sent an email notifying them of a new lead. Set the maximum number of lead acceptance This ensures that the website visitors do not get contacted by dozens of members. Such an experience would be considered as “spam” by most. By setting the limit to “3” for example, the site could technically send out the lead to 50 members but only have a maximum of 3 that can contact the website visitor. More time to focus on marketing The less manual tasks that the team need to complete, the more focus can be used on marketing and sales. Limitations Of Auto-Matching Lower Quality Of Leads There is no way to prevent a solicitation or poor lead from being sent to the members with the auto-matching turned on. Expert Tip Never charge for leads if the auto-matching turned on. Paying for a poor lead is the fastest way to lose members. results.title: The Email Variables Used with the  Leads Module | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: The Email Variables Used with the Leads Module Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008058 The Leads Module includes several variables that can be used when creating or customizing lead-related email templates. These variables allow you to automatically insert lead information, member details, login links, and other dynamic content into your emails. The following variables power the Basic Lead Module, and can be used when creating custom lead emails. Important note: When using lead variables, make sure to enter them exactly as shown below. Some variables require a single percentage sign (%variable%), while others require three percentage signs (%%%variable%%%). Using the wrong format may prevent the variable from displaying correctly in the email. For more information about variables, please see: » Understanding Variables Variables Member Access Variables These variables help members quickly access their account or view a lead. %member_login_link% Automatically logs the member into their dashboard without requiring them to enter their username or password. %member_lead_match_link% Takes the member directly to the specific lead associated with the email without requiring them to log in manually. This is the recommended variable for lead notification emails because it provides the fastest way for members to review, accept, or purchase leads. Lead Information Variables These variables display information submitted by the website visitor when creating the lead. %%%details%%% Displays the lead information fields configured in the Get Matched form. The information displayed by this variable can be customized by editing the fields included in the Get Matched form. %%%lead_id%%% Displays the Lead ID number. This is commonly used in administrative notifications to make it easier to locate a specific lead within the admin area. %%%lead_name%%% Displays the name of the website visitor who submitted the lead. %%%lead_email%%% Displays the email address entered by the website visitor. Important: This variable will display the visitor's email address even if the lead is configured as a Preview Lead. For this reason, it is typically only used in emails sent to the website visitor and is not included in member lead notification emails by default. %%%lead_phone%%% Displays the phone number entered by the website visitor. Like the lead email variable, this will display the phone number regardless of whether the lead is set to Preview or Complete. %%%lead_location%%% Displays the location entered by the website visitor when submitting the lead. Member Information Variables These variables display information about the member who was matched with the lead. %%%full_name%%% Displays the member's name. For Individual Accounts, the member's first and last name will be displayed. For Company Accounts, the company name will be displayed. %%%user_id%%% Displays the member's User ID number. %%%location%%% Displays the location of the matched member. Website Variables %%%website_name%%% Displays the website name. This variable is commonly used in email subject lines and email signatures to reinforce branding and recognition. Security Token Variables These variables return secure system tokens that can be used when creating custom links or integrations. %token% Displays the secure token associated with the lead. %user_token% Displays the secure token associated with the matched member. Custom Login Link Example The following link automatically logs the member into their account and takes them directly to the lead details page: Login to your account to view this lead Additional Information: » How to Edit Email Templates » Emails » Email Templates » New Email Template For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: How to Turn The Brilliant Directories Directory Website into a Mobile Application for Apple & Android | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How to Turn The Brilliant Directories Directory Website into a Mobile Application for Apple & Android Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008202 The video below shows how to convert a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app in less than 5 minutes using third-party, no-code app building platforms. The website users will have the same familiar experience on the mobile app as they do on the main Brilliant Directories website. This approach displays your live website inside an app using WebView technology. Starting with a mobile-friendly website saves time and makes the entire app-building process easier. Video Note The app builder shown in the video (Como) was acquired and later shut down. The same WebView-based approach shown in the video still applies to modern no-code app builders. No-Code Method The easiest way to turn a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app is by using a no-code app builder that supports loading your website inside the app using a WebView. No-code app builders are third-party services and operate independently from Brilliant Directories. They have their own plans, pricing, and publishing requirements. How It Works Your live Brilliant Directories site is displayed inside a mobile app shell. Your homepage loads first, and all navigation, logins, forms, listings, and features work exactly as they do on your website. No content needs to be rebuilt and no code is required. Set your website URL as the app’s homepage, or Add your website as a navigation item within the app Some app builders may show optional menus, screens, or layout tools in their interface. These are not required when using your website as the primary WebView. Limitations This method creates a WebView-based app (a website inside an app). It does not generate a fully custom native mobile app interface. Popular No-Code App Builders Appy Pie Convert your website into Android and iOS apps by entering your site URL. https://www.appypie.com/convert-website-to-mobile-apps BuildFire Embed your website inside the app using the WebView plugin. https://buildfire.com/plugin/webview-2/ GoodBarber Display your website in the app using a URL-based WebView section. https://www.goodbarber.com/help/web-view-sections-r33/url-section-web-view-a27/ NOTE: Any no-code app builder that supports loading a website URL as the app homepage or as a navigation item follows this same general methodology. Advanced Option A fully native mobile app can be built using custom development and the Brilliant Directories API. This approach requires development resources and is outside the scope of no-code app builders. Developer Accounts Publishing a mobile app requires developer accounts with the app stores. These accounts, review processes, and any associated fees are managed directly between you and the app store provider. Apple An Apple Developer account is required to publish apps to the App Store. https://developer.apple.com/support/compare-memberships Google A Google Developer account is required to publish apps to Google Play. http://developer.android.com/distribute/googleplay/start.html For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008873 At any moment, the site can create a subscription (recurring or one-time payment) for a member of the directory. Keep in mind that when someone signs up from the /join page, the system will create the subscription automatically. However, sometimes the owner wants to change the subscription's amount or create a new subscription. This is also very beneficial if the site is taking external payments (bank transfers, checks, etc.,) instead of accepting direct payments on the site. Create a "New Order" Log in to the admin area and navigate to Members » Search Members. Locate the member and click on Actions » Payment History: At the top right, click on the "New Order" button: Fill out the new order form with the subscription details: Membership Plan: Select the membership plan of this specific order. Billing Cycle: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Yearly, and Yearly. (this will depend on the configuration set up in the membership plan) Price Override: Type the new amount for this specific order. Leave this option blank if the membership plan doesn't need to be overridden. Enter a price greater than 0. Start Billing On: By default, the system will show today's date. However, it can be modified to any date in the future. Admin Notes : Add notes for the internal team (See example below). Create Order : The system will save and create the order. Confirm the order by clicking on the "Submit Order" button: The page should load automatically and the message "New Order Created" will appear with an order summary: Card on File If the member had a credit card on file and the date selected was today, then the system should collect the payment. To verify if the money was taken successfully, click on the "Transactions" tab and make sure the status of the order says "Paid". This payment can also be verified under Finance » Transaction History: If the charge couldn't be attempted or there was no card registered to begin with, this means that the credit on file needs to be updated. The unpaid invoice will appear in the "Past Due" tab. When the member updates the credit card on file, the unpaid invoice can be attempted manually. There is no need to create a new order. Manually Collect Payment To attempt the payment manually, click on Actions » Collect Payment: Cash or Bank Transfer If the member paid the invoice by cash or a bank transfer, the invoice can be Marked as Paid at any moment, removing it from the Past Due list. Refunds How to refund a member: How Refunds Work Cancel Subscriptions How to cancel orders: How Do I Cancel Payment Subscriptions - Orders . Update Existing Subscriptions How to update existing member subscriptions: Updating Member Subscriptions For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.content: How to Setup Upgrade/Downgrade Options for Membership Plans Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008978 The Available Upgrade Options settings control which membership plans appear on the Upgrade/Downgrade page for each member. This guide outlines the steps to enable and configure these settings within a Brilliant Directories website. How to Activate the "Available Upgrade Options" Settings Follow these steps: 1. Go to the Membership Plans Section Navigate to Finance » Membership Plans . Click Edit on the membership plan that requires configuration. 2. Open the Sign Ups & Upgrades Tab Click Sign Ups & Upgrades tab. Scroll down to find the section titled Change Plan – Upgrade/Downgrade Settings . Configuration Options Scroll down in the settings area to find the following options: 1. Upgrade Email Sent Choose an email template to send to members after they upgrade to this membership plan. Additional Option Send Copy of Email to Default Website Email Address If checked (default), the system sends a copy of the upgrade email to the site admin. Email Template Recommendations Upgrade Email (Template: upgrade-response ) Use when upgrading from a lower-tier plan. Downgrade Email (Template: downgrade-response ) Use when moving to a lower-tier plan, especially from the highest-tier plan. Generic Template Create a neutral template if this plan is both an upgrade and downgrade option. This keeps the message relevant regardless of direction. 2. After Upgrading to This Plan, Set Account Status As Choose the member's account status after the upgrade Active Account Member becomes active and visible on the site. Inactive Account Member remains inactive and hidden from the site. Same Status Before Upgrading Member retains the status they had before the upgrade. On Hold, Requires Admin Approval Member is on hold until manually approved by the admin. 3. Available Upgrade Options This is the key setting to control which plans members can upgrade or downgrade to. Available Plans Select the membership plans that should appear as upgrade/downgrade options. Pre-Selected Plan Choose the default selected upgrade option. Display Order Choose the order in which plans appear on the upgrade page. 4. Upgrade Page Header Content Enter a custom message or instruction that will appear above the upgrade options on the member’s Upgrade page. 5. Description Why Members Should Upgrade to This Level Add a description that explains the benefits of upgrading to this plan. This description will only be visible to members who are eligible to upgrade to this plan — not to those who are already on it. Note : This message will not display for members already in the plan. This description will not display for members already enrolled in Plan 1. 6. Free Trial when upgrading If the membership plan a member upgrades to includes a Free Trial, the free trial will also be applied during the upgrade process. This means members upgrading to that plan will receive the same trial period as they would during a new sign-up, according to the membership plan's Free Trial settings and this will show in the member dashboard when upgrading: 7. Card-Based Layout on Member Upgrade Page A new Advanced Setting is available to display the available membership plans in a card view instead of the standard list layout. When enabled, members will see the membership plan options presented as individual cards during the sign-up, upgrade, or downgrade process: Additional Notes Membership plans with the Account Type: "Claim" do not allow plan changes until the listing is claimed by a member. results.content: Embed Conversion Tracking and Affiliate Tracking Codes On Sign Up Pages Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009295 There are many 3rd party tools that require placing a tracking code on "success pages" in order to track sales, sign-ups, conversions, and more. With Brilliant Directories, it is possible to place tracking code widget for the "success pages" into each membership plan or in a specific widget that will apply to all membership plans. Membership Plans Method There is a setting on each membership plan where the widget with the code can be placed. It can be found under Finance >> Membership Plans >> find the membership where the code needs to be added and click on Edit . Navigate to the " Sign-Ups & Upgrades " tab and scroll down to " Sign Ups / Upgrade Conversion Tracking Code " and select the preferred widget: *This allows the activation of an additional Tracking Code Widget that will work alongside the default Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes , which will always remain active. Conversion Tracking Codes Widget and Available Variables to Utilize Navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager >> Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes An example conversion tracking to add could look like the following: fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>}); This code should be added below the following comment within this widget: When adding this code, please make sure to wrap it around the <script> tag, as shown below: <script type="text/javascript">fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>});</script> The end result would look like the following: Some common variables that affiliates and other trackers want to be included in the pixel tracking code are the order amount and order or member ID, etc. These are the variables available with Brilliant Directories: COMMON VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE: FIRST PAYMENT AMOUNT = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?> RECURRING PAYMENT AMOUNT = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['recurring_amount']; ?> ORDER ID / MEMBER ID = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['user_id']; ?> COUPON CODE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['coupon_code']; ?> PRODUCT NAME = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_name']; ?> PRODUCT TYPE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_type']; ?> FREE TRIAL = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial']; ?> FREE TRIAL DAYS = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial_period']; ?> FIRST BILL DATE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['first_bill_date']; ?> ADVANCED VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE: $conversion_tracking['invoice']['variable']; (Invoice Variables from the tblinvoices table) $conversion_tracking['product']['variable']; (Member Subscription Variables from the tblhosting table) IMPORTANT NOTE: This widget is where the tracking code for affiliate programs, analytics, and more can be placed. This widget only loads on pages after a member sign-ups or upgrades, to track successful sign-ups. Alternative Method: Adding Conversion Tracking to Pop-Up Success Messages If the conversion action does not load a separate success page (e.g., a pop-up message confirms success on the same page), the conversion tracking code can also be placed in the text label that appears after a successful action. This can be done by navigating the Text Label for the post-success message and embedding the tracking code there. For this example, let's add a Google Ads conversion tracking setup for a newsletter subscriber pop-up. To accomplish this, first, navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager and create a new widget: Name the widget, add the tracking code in the HTML tab, and save the changes: Then copy the PHP shortcode of the widget: Next, place the copied shortcode of the widget to the text label: Alternatively, the code can be inserted directly within the text label. However, we recommend using the widget method for more reliable performance and smoother processing. The tracking code will now trigger each time a user subscribes to the newsletter. This option is especially useful for scenarios where confirmation appears as inline text or a pop-up, rather than a new page. Be sure to use this method as an alternative in any scenario where a separate success page is not available. NOTE : This method may not be optimal and might not work reliably if the script requires a specific loading sequence or is complex. However, it can be effective in many cases. Be sure to thoroughly test before finalizing any updates. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: How Does Auto-Matching Work? (Lead Settings » General Settings) | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How Does Auto-Matching Work? (Lead Settings » General Settings) Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009581 The following documentation is exclusively for the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". Auto-matching relies on the auto-matching settings and the search inputs submitted by the users of the website. Here are some of the core concepts of how auto-matching works: The engine will only match members that match the criteria. If the member is allowed to select a location, say San Francisco, and only 2 members are located in San Francisco, only those two candidates will be matched (assuming they match the additional criteria set by the user such as categories). Membership Level Sort Order is taken into consideration. This means if there are three premium members in San Francisco, these three premium members will always be auto-matched ahead of the free members that are also located in San Francisco. For accurate auto-matching, allowing for category inputs and location inputs is key. Not requiring a location or specialty to be entered limits the engine. Essentially the auto-matching functionality is the same as the member search functionality on the website. The system runs a search just like the users would, and starts to auto-match leads always going from top to bottom. Auto-Matching Lead Settings Edit the auto-matching lead settings by going to Leads » Manage Lead » General Settings : Or within the " Auto-Match Workflows " screen: Data Flows Settings There are 5 additional settings for the automatic matching functionality. Search Radius : Members within this radius are eligible to be automatically matched to leads. Maximum Matches: This setting controls how many members can be matched to a single lead. Set this to "3", and a maximum of 3 members will be matched. If no one meets the search criteria, no one will be matched and the lead will be flagged as "Pending". Maximum Acceptances: This controls how many members can accept a lead. This is particularly helpful if the maximum matches is set to 5+ members, but don't want the website users to be bombarded with emails from the visitors. Once the maximum lead acceptance is reached, the lead status will change to "Sold Out". Notify Admin If Member Email Invalid: Select "Yes" if you would like to send an email notification to the Admin when a lead has been matched to a member that does not have a valid email address. Admin Notification Email Template: Select the email template to send to the Admin if a lead is matched to a member that does not have a valid email address. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.content: Understanding Actions / Data Flows Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009585 This documentation covers features specific to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on. Automatic Lead Matching Add-On What Is It? The Automatic Lead Matching add-on upgrades the default Leads system by introducing customizable Lead Actions—rules that control how leads are handled for different membership levels. The standard Basic Leads Package includes: Instant delivery for direct lead requests Limit on how many members can accept a lead Admin email alerts when new leads come in With this add-on, custom Lead Actions can be created and assigned to individual membership levels, giving full control over how leads are distributed and managed. Key Features: Auto-Match Control: Decide which members can receive leads automatically. Custom Email Templates per Membership Level : Send different email content to free vs. paid members—thank paying members and encourage free users to upgrade. Member Lead Acceptance Alerts : Get notified when a member accepts a lead—ideal timing to follow up or promote upgrades. Automate a thank-you or upsell email. Sold-Out Lead Notifications: Get alerted when a member tries to claim a lead that’s already been sold. Trigger an automatic email explaining what happened and how to avoid it. These features are exclusive to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on and designed to help automate lead distribution while maximizing upsell opportunities and overall lead management efficiency. results.title: Managing Member Credit Cards | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Managing Member Credit Cards Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000011521 This article covers how to do the following from the Admin area of the site: How to check if a member currently has a credit card on file. How to add a credit card for a member. How to update the credit card on file for a member. How to delete a credit card on file for a member. To do any of the above actions, follow these steps: Click My Members » Search Members Search for the member and click Actions » Payment History: Click the "CC Info" button: Checking if a Member Has a Credit Card on File If the member has a credit card on file, a snippet of the credit card information will display here: Adding a Credit Card for a Member Click the "Add Credit Card" button: Enter the credit card information of the member: Click the "Save credit card & continue" button. If the complete credit card information is entered with no errors, a success message like this will appear: Click the "Close Window" button. The member's credit card information on file will be displayed here: Understanding Card Type Information (Stripe Only) When an admin views a member’s saved payment information in the member’s Account Details , the dashboard will also display the type of card stored for that account. This information is only available when when Stripe is used as the payment gateway. Other gateways do not display these details. The card type label helps clarify how the card is stored in Stripe and whether it supports recurring subscription payments. Below are the possible types and their meanings: Legacy A non-3D Secure card saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe. Legacy (3DS) A 3D Secure card saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe . If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe. Payment Method A non-3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe. This is Stripe's preferred, most up-to-date format. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. Payment Method (3DS Recurring) A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that supports recurring subscription payments. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. Payment Method (3DS Manual) A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that requires manual authentication for each transaction. The member must log in to their Member Dashboard and manually authenticate every payment. The member may contact the bank to remove this requirement or use a different card. The current credit card on file will appear at the top of the modal. The fields for entering the updated information will also appear there: Click the "Save credit card & continue" button. If the complete credit card information is entered with no errors , a success message like this will display: Click the "Close Window" button. The updated credit card information will be reflected on the following page: Updating a Member’s Credit Card on File Click the "Clear" button: Confirm removal of the credit card on file by clicking the "Yes, clear credit card" button: Once successfully deleted, a success message will appear, click the "Close Window" button: Customizing Member Credit Card Form Text Labels The text labels displayed in the pop-up for adding or updating a member’s credit card can be modified in the Admin area. results.title: Edit 404 Error Pages | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Edit 404 Error Pages Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000012124 When a requested URL does not correspond to an existing page on the website, the server returns a “404 Not Found” error, indicating that the page cannot be located. Common triggers for this error include: A visitor clicks a link on another site that leads to a non-existent page on the directory. A URL that previously existed has been deleted or moved. A visitor mistypes a URL. A bot or crawler (such as from Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, etc.) attempts to access a URL in error. When any of these events occur, the website responds with the 404 error code and displays a designated “404 error page” (the content served when the page cannot be found). How to Create a Custom 404 Page Navigate to My Content >> New Web Page Add a unique Permalink (e.g., "my404") Set the page type as “ Single Web Page ”. Save the page. Once created, the 404 page can be styled and populated with whatever content and links are appropriate for the site. Alternatively, ask the BD Butler to create a unique 404 page design. Selecting the Default 404 Error Page Within the platform’s advanced settings, there is an option labelled Default 404 Error Page . Using the dropdown menu, select the newly created web page (or any existing page) to serve as the designated 404 error page. Default 404 Error Page error_404 How Does a Brilliant Directories Website Handle 404 Error Pages? Historically, all Brilliant Directories-powered websites used the homepage as the 404 error page. While using the homepage can work for human visitors (because they can potentially find their destination via the homepage), the homepage is typically one of the heaviest pages in terms of bandwidth—often loading multiple megabytes. When non-human traffic (such as bots or crawlers) triggers 404 errors and is served the homepage each time, this can consume excessive bandwidth and server resources. To mitigate this, the system now uses a minimal default 404 error page that: Presents a simple notification that the requested page cannot be found. Includes a link to the homepage for genuine users who may wish to continue browsing. Uses significantly less bandwidth (on the order of ~1 KB) compared to loading the full homepage. This change helps reduce unnecessary server load arising from erroneous URL requests while still providing a user-friendly experience for legitimate visitors. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? In this case, the error was caused by a blocked spam word, so the exact word will be displayed in the description: There are other errors that may prevent account creation. results.title: How Bandwidth and Storage Usage Is Calculated | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How Bandwidth and Storage Usage Is Calculated Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000013438 In the Dashboard Area of every Brilliant Directories website, there is an indication of the storage that is currently being used and the bandwidth that has been used for the current calendar month: Our server network utilizes the CentOS / WHM / cPanel stack to manage hosting accounts and calculate bandwidth and storage usage data. To measure bandwidth, cPanel & WHM combines the amount of bytes of an incoming data request with the outgoing transferred data (the response to that request). cPanel & WHM obtains this data from the Apache logs. These logs include the following amounts of bandwidth: The total bandwidth that the incoming request that solicited the content used. The total bandwidth that the complete response used (the sum of the size of the content plus the header). For more information about how bandwidth usage data is calculated, and why it may differ from data obtained using other tools, please see the full documentation on this topic here: Apparent Discrepancies in Bandwidth Usage Statistics For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: How To Enable Hotlink Protection | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How To Enable Hotlink Protection Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000013802 Understanding Hotlink Protection Hotlinking occurs when another website displays files that are hosted on your website, such as images, by directly linking to their source URL. While the content appears on the third-party website, the files are still being served from your website, which means your website's bandwidth and server resources are being used to deliver that content. How Hotlink Protection Works Hotlink protection prevents other websites from directly embedding and displaying files hosted on your website. When enabled, requests originating from unauthorized domains will be blocked from accessing protected content. This can help reduce unnecessary bandwidth usage and prevent third-party websites from using your hosted images and files without permission. Important Considerations Before enabling hotlink protection, keep in mind that some websites and services may no longer be able to display your images if they rely on direct file access. Many major platforms, including social media networks, use their own methods to preview and cache content, so they are generally not affected. However, smaller websites and applications that directly reference your image URLs may be unable to display those files once hotlink protection is enabled. Option 1: Enable Hotlink Protection with Cloudflare If your website is connected to Cloudflare, you can enable Cloudflare's built-in Hotlink Protection feature. Cloudflare Documentation: https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200170026-Understanding-Cloudflare-Hotlink-Protection Option 2: Configure Hotlink Protection with an .htaccess File For websites hosted on servers that support Apache configuration files, hotlink protection can also be implemented using rules added to the website's .htaccess file. Reference Guide: https://mediatemple.net/community/products/dv/204644230/prevent-hotlinking-with-a-.htaccess-file Additional Notes Brilliant Directories does not currently include a built-in hotlink protection setting. If hotlink protection is required, it will need to be configured through a service such as Cloudflare or by implementing server-level rules where supported. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: Manage Your Website's Email Accounts With Microsoft 365 | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Manage Your Website's Email Accounts With Microsoft 365 Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000014019 Manage a Website's Email Accounts with Microsoft 365 Microsoft 365 can host email for a domain connected to a Brilliant Directories website. Microsoft supplies the DNS records that verify the domain and route mail to its service. 1. Add and Verify the Domain in Microsoft 365 Open Settings > Domains in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Add the root domain without www . Copy the TXT verification record supplied by Microsoft. Add that record wherever the domain's live DNS is managed, then complete Microsoft's verification. Microsoft references: Add a custom domain and add DNS records at a DNS provider . 2. Find Where DNS Is Managed If the domain uses Brilliant Directories-managed DNS, open Settings > Domain Manager . Hosted email routing is available under Mailboxes ; see Manage Mailboxes and Email Routing . DNS records can also be managed through Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard > Zone Editor when that option is available. If the domain uses Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap, or another provider's nameservers, add the Microsoft records at that provider. Records added in cPanel do not affect a domain whose live DNS is hosted elsewhere. 3. Add the Microsoft 365 Records Copy the exact values from the Microsoft 365 admin center. Common records include: Type Common host Purpose TXT @ or root Verifies domain ownership. MX @ or root Routes incoming mail to Microsoft 365. CNAME autodiscover Helps Outlook locate mailbox settings. TXT @ or root Authorizes Microsoft 365 in SPF. Microsoft can also require CNAME or SRV records for Teams, device enrollment, and other services. Add only the records displayed for the domain and enabled services. See Microsoft's external DNS record reference . 4. Change Mail Routing Create the Microsoft 365 mailboxes before changing MX. Replace obsolete MX records with the Microsoft value and priority shown in the admin center. Leaving conflicting MX records can split or misdirect incoming mail. Microsoft 365 requires the exact mail server hostname supplied in its admin center. Opening this form does not change routing. 5. Configure SPF A domain should publish one SPF TXT record. If SPF already exists, merge the required authorized senders into that record instead of adding a second SPF record. Follow Microsoft's SPF guidance . 6. Verify and Test Use Microsoft's record check, then test sending and receiving. If verification fails, confirm the host/name, destination, priority, spaces, duplicate SPF records, old MX records, and the authoritative DNS provider. Service Boundaries Microsoft manages its mailboxes, billing, passwords, and account access. Brilliant Directories provides DNS or routing controls only when the domain uses supported Brilliant Directories-managed services. results.title: Setting Up How Member Reviews Are Approved On The Website | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Setting Up How Member Reviews Are Approved On The Website Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000014153 To configure how member reviews are approved on your website, go to: Finance » Membership Plans » Profile Page Tab . The review approval workflow is controlled by two settings: Require All Reviews To Be Approved by Admin First – Determines whether an administrator must review and approve new reviews before they can be published. Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member) – Determines whether members can approve or reject reviews submitted to their profile. The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below. The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below. Scenario 1 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO NO Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO NO By setting both to "NO", all member reviews that are submitted to the website will automatically get published and appear live on the member's profile page and the homepage if the latest reviews are streamed. Scenario 2 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO NO Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO YES Scenario 2 automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The review will not be published on the website until the member approves the review. The member will also receive an automated notification that there is a pending review in their account. Scenario 3 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO YES Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO YES The third scenario automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". The admin gets an email notification that a review was submitted and must go to the admin area of the website to approve the review manually. » Approving Member Reviews from the Admin Scenario 4 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO YES Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO NO Our last scenario automatically sets reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". Since members are not able to accept or delete reviews, the admin only has the choice to accept or delete the review. There is no option to notify the member or set it to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The ADMIN will see the following pop-up when the setting is changed to "APPROVED" » Approving Member Reviews from the Admin Email Templates Linked To New Review Module Depending on your review approval settings, different email templates may be sent to the reviewer or the site administrator. These templates can be customized under Emails → Email Templates . admin-review-notification update-pending-reviews For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Toolbox » Sidebar Applications | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Toolbox » Sidebar Applications Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000018932 What is a Sidebar A sidebar is a container that holds widgets, typically displayed to the side of web pages. Common examples of widgets placed in sidebars include banner ads, search modules, and newsletter signup modules. The Brilliant Directories platform comes with a set of predefined sidebars that can be modified and updated according to the website's needs. Sidebar Examples Post Details Pages: Static Pages: Member Search Results: Additional Information: Sidebar Setup Steps For Membership Features/ Post Types How To Add A Sidebar To A Static Page How To Create A Sidebar This is IMPORTANT INFORMATION about Sidebars: Sidebars are containers, not positioning tools. A sidebar simply wraps around a group of widgets that will be used together. Despite the name, a sidebar does not place its widgets on the left or right side of a page; that placement comes from CSS applied on the page where the sidebar is used. Any sidebar can be called with a shortcode. To use a sidebar on a static page, or on any page that does not offer a built-in sidebar option (as the membership features do), add the shortcode with the sidebar's name. For example, for a sidebar named myCustomSidebar, add [ sidebar = name_sidebar ] to the page, placing the code closest to where the sidebar should appear. If needed, style it with CSS to look correct or to mimic a sidebar on a different page. The same sidebar can look different on different pages. Because sidebars carry no positioning CSS of their own, using a sidebar on one page does not guarantee it will look the same on another. results.content: How to Connect a Domain to a Brilliant Directories Website Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019271 Connect a custom domain, a subdomain, or a free directoryup.com address from Settings > Domain Manager . The connection flow checks the proposed address and shows the pointing instructions before changing the website address. Example on a free directoryup.com address. Additional tabs appear when a custom domain and its services are available. About the examples: The screenshots use Brilliant Directories test websites. demotailwind.com is managed in Cloudflare and illustrates the Cloudflare route; selfautomated.com uses Brilliant Directories nameservers and illustrates the non-Cloudflare alternative. These are alternative DNS arrangements, not consecutive changes to the same domain. Before starting For a custom domain, have access to its DNS provider and registrar. Record the existing mail provider and preserve its MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and other required records. For a Cloudflare connection, have permission to authorize the correct account and domain. For an existing live site, complete the domain-change checklist . Managed SSL installation requires the Managed SSL add-on to be active. A domain change alone does not add that entitlement. Choose the correct site before starting. The final switch changes the website address. The former address is no longer the site’s primary address, and an old-domain redirect must be arranged separately if needed. The wizard has four stages, shown across the top: Choose An Address , Check It , Point Domain , and Switch Over . A completed stage can be clicked to return to it until the switch has run. 1. Choose An Address Open Settings > Domain Manager > Domain . Click Connect my domain name or Change my domain name . Select the appropriate option below. Use a domain from my Cloudflare account : when available, authorize Cloudflare and select a domain from the account. The screen marks this option Fastest — nothing to type . A domain name I own : enter a registered domain or a true subdomain and configure its DNS. A free address from us : choose the portion before .directoryup.com . Choose the route that matches the domain and DNS provider. 2. Check It Enter the address without http:// , https:// , or a page path. A root domain can be typed with or without www., as example.com or www.example.com . The wizard always connects a root domain as www.example.com . A true subdomain is entered exactly, such as members.example.com . If www. is typed in front of a subdomain, the wizard removes it and checks the subdomain itself. For a root domain, choose how the address appears under How should your address appear? : With www. or Without www. . The choice appears as soon as a root domain is typed, and its default follows what was typed. Visitors who type the other version are sent to the chosen one. Without www. needs the root domain itself to point at the website; see Point the root domain . Click Check this address . The box turns green when the address can be checked. A domain extension that does not exist, such as .come , is refused with a message naming it. Resolve any validation message before continuing. For a free address, enter only the chosen prefix using letters, numbers, and hyphens. For Cloudflare, select the intended domain from the account's domain list; use its filter to locate the correct domain. The A domain name I own route: a root domain is typed and the With www. / Without www. choice appears under the box. The Cloudflare route selects the domain from a list instead, as shown below. 3. Point Domain The Point Domain stage reports where the address currently points, names the company where the records are added (the domain's DNS provider, or the registrar when no DNS provider is identified), and lists each record with its own Pointed or Not pointed yet status. Copy the site's own target from this screen; an example address from documentation is not a usable target. Instructions opens the step-by-step guide below the records, and Use a different address returns to Check It . Add the records at the current DNS provider Open the DNS provider's record editor. Add or update the record for the exact host shown in the wizard. Save the DNS change at the provider. Return to Domain Manager. Click Check again . The www record has these fields: Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target copied from Domain Manager For a subdomain such as members.example.com , the only record is a CNAME whose name is normally members at the DNS provider, pointing to the same target. The root domain is not changed. For a root domain, the stage lists a second entry for example.com itself: a record, or a forwarding setting on GoDaddy with With www. . With With www. , that entry sends visitors who type example.com on to www.example.com; the website works at www.example.com without it, so Continue is offered once the www record is pointed. With Without www. , example.com is the main address and must reach the website. The root domain cannot take an ordinary CNAME, so the right record depends on the DNS provider; see Point the root domain . The Point Domain stage for a subdomain of a domain in the connected Cloudflare account. Use the target shown by the website being connected. Point the root domain (CNAME exception) DNS does not allow an ordinary CNAME record on the root of a domain (the record named @ ), so the root domain is connected differently depending on the company that runs the domain's DNS. The Point Domain stage identifies that company from the domain's nameservers and shows the matching method below: a CNAME on Cloudflare, Domain Forwarding on GoDaddy when the address uses www, an ALIAS record on Namecheap, and an A record for any other DNS provider or when the provider cannot be identified. An A record works everywhere, but it points at a fixed server address; the Cloudflare, GoDaddy, and Namecheap methods keep the domain following the website if it moves to a different server. Brilliant Directories nameservers Nothing needs to be added. The Point Domain stage reports We manage the DNS for the address, and the records are created during the switch. Cloudflare Cloudflare flattens a CNAME on the root, so the root takes the same record as www. Delete the existing root and www records first, then add both of these: Type: CNAME Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target When the Cloudflare account is connected to Domain Manager, Use a domain from my Cloudflare account or Add this record for me creates these records automatically. GoDaddy GoDaddy does not allow a CNAME record on the root of a domain. With With www. , connect it in two steps: Edit the existing www record so it is a CNAME pointing to the site's unique directoryup.com target. Turn on Domain Forwarding so example.com forwards to https://www.example.com : in GoDaddy's DNS settings for the domain, open Forwarding , click Add Forwarding , choose https:// , enter www.example.com , select Permanent (301) , and click Save . GoDaddy's Forwarding settings: forward the root domain to the https www address, permanently (301). The Point Domain stage shows this forwarding in place of a root record, with a link to GoDaddy's guide. Once example.com forwards permanently (301) to https://www.example.com, the root domain reads Pointed on the Point Domain and Switch Over stages. With Without www. , do not turn on Domain Forwarding for the root domain: the website already sends www visitors to example.com, so a forward the other way sends visitors in a circle and the site stops loading. Add an A record for the root instead, alongside the www CNAME: Type: A Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. Namecheap Namecheap supports an ALIAS record on the root of a domain. Namecheap does not allow an ALIAS record alongside an existing A, AAAA, CNAME, or redirect record for the same host, so delete the current root domain record first, then use Add New Record to create: Type: ALIAS Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Namecheap's guide: How to create an ALIAS record . Other DNS providers Add the www CNAME above, and an A record for the root domain: Type: A Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. For the long term, moving the domain's DNS to a free Cloudflare account avoids this, because Cloudflare can hold the site's target on the root domain; see Connecting a Site to Cloudflare . Use a connected Cloudflare account After Cloudflare authorization, filter the domain list and select the intended domain. Choose its main www. address or enter a subdomain, then click Use this address . The wizard prepares the DNS records and advances to Switch Over , skipping the Point Domain stage. To see the record it added, click Show me the DNS record you added on the Switch Over stage. Start over returns to the three choices. A domain entered through A domain name I own can also be on Cloudflare. When the domain is in the Cloudflare zone already connected to the site, the Point Domain stage offers Add this record for me . When it is on Cloudflare under a different zone or account, the stage offers Set it up for me , or Sign in and set it up for me when the account holding that domain is not connected yet. Use the offered button, or expand I would rather add the record myself to add the record by hand, then click Check again . Preparing a record does not complete the website-address switch; the final confirmation is still required. See Cloudflare in Domain Manager . Filter the Cloudflare domain list, select the intended domain, and choose the main address or a subdomain. Move the entire domain's DNS to Brilliant Directories The nameserver alternative is appropriate when the whole domain's DNS should be managed by Brilliant Directories. It is not necessary merely to connect one subdomain. On the Point Domain stage, select Nameservers instead of DNS record to show the two nameservers, then replace the domain's nameservers at the registrar with both of them: Nameserver: ns1.directorysecure.com Nameserver: ns2.directorysecure.com When the domain already uses these nameservers, the Point Domain stage reports We manage the DNS for the address. There is nothing to add; the record is created during the switch. A nameserver change can take a few hours to reach everyone. A nameserver change affects the whole domain. The wizard warns that this moves all DNS to Brilliant Directories. Preserve and recreate the records required by existing email and other services before changing nameservers. For a single subdomain while the main website or email stays elsewhere, use the subdomain CNAME route. Free directoryup.com addresses do not need records changed at an external registrar; their flow skips the Point Domain stage. Non-Cloudflare example: selfautomated.com is registered at GoDaddy and uses Brilliant Directories nameservers. The Domain tab confirms that both the main address and the address without www are connected. 4. Switch Over Click Continue after reviewing the pointing result. When the main address is not pointed yet, this button reads Continue anyway . Check Now and After the change . After the change lists the main address first and, for a root domain, the other version with forwards to . Each shows its own status: Pointed , Cannot verify , Checking… , or Not pointed yet . Click Not pointed yet to see what is missing; Show me what to set up returns to Point Domain . Read the message above the buttons. Ready to switch to the new address appears when it is ready; otherwise What happens when you switch describes the change. Both name the current address, which stops loading the website once the switch is done. Click Switch to this address . Confirm Yes, switch it in the confirmation dialog. Keep the page open until the progress screen completes. Do not treat a Not pointed yet result as a completed connection. Continue anyway allows the switch before DNS is ready: the new address does not load the website until its record is in place, and the current address stops working straight away. If Without www. was chosen but the root domain does not reach the website yet, the switch keeps the website on the www version and Domain Manager says so. Change it later under Web address style once the root domain points at the website; see Set Up The WWW or Non-WWW Version Of The Domain . Review the current and new addresses and the message above the buttons before confirming the switch. Confirm the result The completion screen identifies the new address and the remaining setup tasks. Email authentication is attempted during the switch when the connected DNS service can accept the records. If manual setup is required, follow the Emails tab's instructions. Managed SSL installation is attempted when the add-on is active; certificate issuance can finish after the address change. The switch also moves the website's sending address to the new domain when it used the old domain or a placeholder address, keeping the part before the @. An address at another domain, such as a Gmail address, is left unchanged. The completed switch identifies the new address and the remaining SSL and integration tasks. Website sender authentication is separate from incoming-mail setup. Open the new website address. Review the SSL tab. Review Emails > Sender Authentication . Test website forms, login, and any domain-restricted integrations. DNS changes can take time to become visible everywhere. Use Check again and compare the exact host and target if the connection remains unresolved. Contact support with the domain, site ID, and displayed error when the records appear correct but the site still fails. Free-address testing has separate limitations; see directoryup.com Subdomain Test Credentials . For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019275 IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless the site has heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use around the website. This article will cover the image settings for the following: Profile Photo for Website Profile Photo for Social Media Sharing Profile Logo for Website Profile Logo for Social Media Sharing Profile Cover On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the Member Photos , Member Logos and Cover Photos sections, listed under Image Sizes in the side menu. Changes on the Image Settings page take effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar at the top of the page. 1 — the Member Photos, Member Logos and Cover Photos sections in the side menu. 2 — the settings of the selected section. Additional Information: Image Settings - Member Post Types- Single Photo Image Settings - Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Profile Logo Settings Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Logo: The profile logo can be set to either an “Open” ratio or a fixed aspect ratio of 3:4 or 1:1 . More details on how aspect ratios work can be found here. When selecting the “Open” option, members are not restricted to a specific shape. This means they can upload images that are square, wider than they are tall, or taller than they are wide. With the ratio set to “Open” , the Width and Height values act as maximum limits rather than fixed dimensions. For example, if both values are set to 200px and a member uploads a 2000px × 2000px image, the system will automatically resize it to 200px × 200px . The image’s original proportions are preserved, but it is scaled down so it does not exceed the defined limits. This resizing helps ensure that images remain optimized for performance, allowing pages to load faster and improving the overall browsing experience across the website. 1 — the Profile Logo setting. 2 — its Ratio, which can be Open, 1:1 or 3:4. Entering a "Profile Logo" width of less than 162px shows a Warning message, and the width is reset to 162px: *This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where profile logos are used. Entering a "Profile Logo Social Media" width or height of less than the required 200px shows a Warning message, and the value is reset to 200px: Profile Photo Settings The Profile Photo Settings function much like the Profile Logo Settings, with one key difference; Profile Photos allow you to set an aspect ratio of 3:4 or 1:1. This helps ensure that profile images fit properly across different areas of the website where they are displayed. Please note: Changing the default Aspect Ratios is possible, but not recommended. Doing so would require customizing the design of the website significantly in order to accommodate a different aspect ratio for these images around the website and should only be requested by Advanced Users of the software that have significant experience in customizing the design of Brilliant Directories websites. Profile Cover Settings Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Cover: The ratio of the Profile Cover will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide. Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image. For example, if the Width and height are set to 1200px x 500px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 800px tall, the final image will be resized to be 1 200px wide x 500px tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the limit. This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible. How To Upload Logo Images As A Member Login as a member and go to the "Profile Photo" Tab Click on "Upload Logo" (once a logo has been uploaded, the button reads "Change Logo"): NOTE: Accepted Image formats are: JPG, PNG, GIF and WEBP 3. Click "Choose Logo" and select an image to upload. It opens in the cropping window: 4. Click "Click to Save Photo". If the logo is not large enough the member will receive the following message, warning them that the current image is smaller than 200px x 200px and will have to be stretched in order to meet the minimum size requirements for sharing on social media websites, and the logo will appear on the website at a smaller size than other Profile Logos. This warning appears only when the Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning. How To Upload Profile Photos As A Member When uploading the profile photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Logo. However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the 3:4 Aspect Ratio specified in the Profile Photo Settings: If the photo is smaller than 200px x 200px, clicking "Click to Save Photo" shows the following warning, and "Upload and Stretch" uploads it anyway. This warning appears only when the Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning. It is now possible to zoom in & out , rotate , and flip profile photo images while cropping, using the tools below the image: How To Upload Cover Images As A Member When uploading the cover photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Picture/Logo. However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the dimensions specified in the Profile Cover Settings : Additional Information The image module is made up of text labels that can be edited: » How to locate Text Labels on the Front end of a Website » Settings » Text Labels For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019276 IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless doing heavy customizations to the underlying code of a website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use on a Brilliant Directories website. This article will cover the image settings for the following: Single Photo Post - Thumbnail Single Photo Post - Large On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the Single Photo Posts section, listed under Image Sizes in the side menu. Changes on the Image Settings page take effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar at the top of the page. 1 — Single Photo Posts in the side menu. 2 — the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail and Single Photo Post - Large settings. We also have the following articles available that cover the other sections: Image Settings - Profile Photos & Logos Image Settings - Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Default Member Post Types That These Settings Apply To These settings apply to all member post types where one photo can be added to a single post. These post types include: Member Article Blog Article Event Coupon Jobs Single Photo Post - Thumbnail Settings This setting determines the maximum dimensions that single-photo member post type will have when viewed in most locations around the website (homepage streaming widgets, member profile pages, and search results). The only place this setting does not apply is the Details page of the post (the single page devoted to the full post) . The setting for the size of the photo on the Details page of the post is set by the " Single Photo Post - Large" setting (see section below). The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 272, and a height of 160. The ratio of the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - it can be square, wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide. Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image. For example, if both the Width and Height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 2000px tall, the final image will be resized to be 200px wide x 200px tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the 200px x 200px limit. This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible. As another example, if both the Width and height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 1000px tall, the image will be resized so that it fits within the limits of 200px x 200px, without changing the aspect ratio. In this example, the final uploaded image would be 200px wide x 100px tall so it fits within the 200px x 200px limit without changing its aspect ratio or stretching / distorting the image. If the "Single Photo Post - Thumbnail" width is set to less than 160px, a Warning message appears and the width is reset to 160px: ** This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where single photo member post type thumbnails are used. Even though images can be set to be smaller than the default settings, we do not recommend doing so unless customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these smaller images. The Width and Height settings can be set as high as needed, but please note doing this will not cause the images to DISPLAY larger around the site, The image itself will be saved at a larger size, but will be shrunk down to fit into the space available for it when displayed on the website. In other words, all of the images will take longer and use more bandwidth to load, and will not display any larger on the website. Making these images larger will only be useful if heavily customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these larger images. Single Photo Post - Large Settings This setting determines the maximum dimensions that single-photo member posts type will have when viewed on the Details page of the post (the single page devoted to the full post). The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 375, and a height of 375. This is also the image used when sharing the Details page of the post on social media. A single image post will have the Image Upload field directly on the form: Recommended Size : 750 by 400 pixels The recommended size text is a text label. System Variable : recommended_size_single_photo The articles below will explain how to upload these types of posts: » How to Post an Event » How to Post a Coupon » How to Post a Community Article » How to Post a Job Offer For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Developer Hub » Image Settings | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Developer Hub » Image Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019278 What are the Image Settings? The Image Settings of the website determine the final size that images will be saved after being uploaded to the website by members. The default settings that come with a Brilliant Directories website are designed so that images will fit well in all of the areas of the website in which they display while being optimized for load speed and meeting minimum requirements for social media sharing. IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless doing heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use on a Brilliant Directories website. How to Access the Image Settings Go to ADMIN » DEVELOPER HUB and click Edit Image Sizes on the Image Settings card: Using the Image Settings Page The page lists every image size in one place, grouped into sections: Search — type part of a setting's name to show only the matching settings. The number of results appears below the box, and Clear (or the X in the box) shows every setting again. Side menu — click a section to jump to it. The Image Sizes group holds Member Photos , Member Logos , Cover Photos , Single Photo Posts , Album Posts and Text Editor Images . The Page Speed group holds Lazy Loading . Settings — each section lists its image sizes with a Width and Height in pixels, plus a Ratio for the member photo and logo sizes. Restore Defaults — puts every image size and the lazy loading setting back to the platform defaults (see below). Searching for a setting: Saving Changes Changes on this page are not saved until Save is clicked. As soon as a value changes, the edited setting is marked with a dot and a save bar appears at the top of the page with the message Unsaved changes and two buttons: Save — saves every change on the page at once, including the Lazy Loading setting. The button briefly shows Saved when the save is complete. Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) does the same while the save bar is showing. Discard — asks Discard Unsaved Changes? and, after Discard Changes is clicked, puts back the values that were last saved. Keep Editing closes the question without losing anything. Changing a size and then discarding the change: Some values are checked as they are entered. A width or height below the minimum allowed for that image (EG 162 pixels for the Profile Logo width) shows a Warning message and the value is reset to the minimum. The articles linked at the end of this page cover the limits for each image size. Restore Defaults Clicking Restore Defaults asks for confirmation first. After Restore Defaults is clicked in the confirmation, every image size goes back to its recommended size and Lazy Load Images goes back to Load Images After Scroll . These values are saved right away , with no separate Save step, and the website uses the new sizes immediately. Click Cancel to leave the settings unchanged. General Image Settings Information Lazy Loading ( Load Images After Scroll / Load Images After Page Load / Disabled ) The Lazy Load Images setting is in the Lazy Loading section, under Page Speed in the side menu. Like every other setting on the page, a new choice takes effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar. 1 — Lazy Loading in the side menu, under Page Speed. 2 — the Lazy Load Images setting. Lazy Loading is a set of techniques in web and application development that defers the loading of resources on a page to a later point in time—when those resources are actually needed instead of loading them upfront. These techniques help in improving performance, better utilization of the device’s resources, and reducing associated costs with bandwidth consumption. Load Images After Scroll: Images will only start loading once the page scrolls showing new data and images (Best bandwidth consumption efficiency) Load Images After Page Load: Once the first images Above the fold are loaded, it starts loading images below the fold (quickly loads pages, but consumes more bandwidth) Best for Carousels and Streaming Widgets. Disabled: Loads all images by default. Ratio The "Ratio" refers to the Aspect Ratio of the image, which is how large the height of an image will be relative to the width of the image and vice-versa. For example, a 1:1 aspect ratio means it will be a square - for every 1 pixel of width, the image will have 1 pixel of height. As another example, the Aspect Ratio of an HD television is 16:9 (a rectangle that is wider than it is tall), meaning the image on the television will have 16 pixels of width for every 9 pixels of height. An "Open" aspect ratio means there is no set aspect ratio at all, meaning the image can be any shape. For more information about Aspect Ratios, please see the Wikipedia article on the topic . Width The maximum width of the final image in pixels. Height The maximum height of the final image in pixels. Social Media Sharing When uploading an image, two copies of the image will be saved: one that is optimized for display on the website, and one that is optimized for social media sharing. Currently, Facebook and many other popular social media sites require images to be at least 200px x 200px to be shared on their platform. One copy of the image will be saved to be at least this size, and another will be saved that is optimized for displaying on the website where a smaller size is required. Adding Images for Members Users can upload Logos and Profile Photos through the member dashboard: How to Complete a Profile as a Member Admins can import members with Logos and Profile Photos through the import file: Importing Members with Images These images are added as links into an import file that is uploaded and then added to the corresponding member profile. Using links to add member Logos and Profile Photos is only available through the member import file. Specific Image Settings Information For more information about the settings available on this page as they apply to different areas of the site, check out the following articles: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Developer Hub » Image Settings » Froala Text Editor Images For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard .
