results.content: Migrate City - Zip Code Service Areas - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109028 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What Migrate City - Zip Code Service Areas Does This installer fills in missing city and zip code values on the service areas the site's members have saved. A service area is a location a member selects in their account to show where they work, either a city or a zip code. Older records stored each area's map coordinates but not its city name or zip code as text. This update looks each incomplete area up with Google's Geocoding service and writes the missing value onto the record. Specifically, when the step runs it: Finds every record in the service_areas table where a City-type area has an empty city value or a Zip-type area has an empty zip code value. Groups those records by place, so each unique location is looked up only once even when many members selected the same area. Sends each place to Google's Geocoding API (using its Google place ID where available, falling back to its address or its coordinates) and reads the city name and postal code from the result. Saves the values back to the database through the Bootstrap Theme - Account - Select Locations widget, updating every member record that shares that place. One cleanup action happens automatically during the status check itself, before anything is clicked: the installer deletes service-area rows that have both an empty place ID and an empty address. Those rows carry no location information at all. With no place ID and no address, nothing identifies which location the row was ever meant to represent, so it cannot be looked up, shown on a profile, or matched in a search. Removing these rows clears junk data and does not touch any real area a member selected. Why It Appears It appears when at least one saved service area is missing its city name (for City-type areas) or its zip code (for Zip-type areas). This is an age-related condition: these text fields were added to the platform later, so areas saved before then have them empty, while newly saved areas include the values from the start. Two prerequisites must also be met before the step offers its button: A Google Maps API key must be saved in the website settings. Every lookup in this migration goes through Google's Geocoding API, and without a key the step shows a red error message instead of a button and cannot run. The newer service-area database columns must already exist. They are added by the Multi-Location Add-on installer; if they are missing, this step shows an error asking for that update to be run first. Why It Matters The city and zip code values identify each service area by name rather than only by map coordinates, and they are the same values the platform saves for newly selected areas. Completing the migration brings the older records up to that same standard, so every member's service areas are stored consistently. This is a data-completeness update: it does not change the website's design or any member-entered content, it fills in blanks on existing location records. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, Migrate City - Zip Code Service Areas appears in the list. Click its Perform Step button. After it completes, click Check For Updates again — the entry disappears once all steps are done. If Migrate City - Zip Code Service Areas does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. Unlike most installers, this one runs interactively in the browser, which is why its button is labeled Perform Step . Clicking it opens a progress dialog with a small map, a running total of areas fetched, and a count of batches left. Keep the browser tab open while it works through the lookups; when everything is saved, a confirmation appears and the page reloads. Each lookup uses the Google Maps API key, so a large migration counts against that key's Geocoding usage quota. If Google reports that the usage limit was reached, the page waits 10 minutes and reloads automatically, then continues with the areas that are still missing values. Progress is saved place by place, so nothing is lost if the page reloads partway through. After Running When the dialog finishes it confirms that all coordinates were saved and the page reloads. Click Check For Updates again; the entry disappears once no service areas are missing a city or zip code. The site's members' saved areas are unchanged apart from the newly filled-in city and zip code values, and no member action is needed. If the dialog reports an error while saving, make sure the Bootstrap Theme - Account - Select Locations widget on the site is updated to its latest version, then run the step again. Areas that were already updated keep their values, and the step continues with only the records still missing data. This update adds new database columns so each of those records can describe an actual region with a name, instead of just a single point on the map. Specifically, it adds up to six columns to the service_areas table, checking each one individually and creating only the ones that are missing: nelat , nelng , swlat , swlng : numeric coordinates for the northeast and southwest corners of the area's bounding box, the rectangle that outlines the area on a map (these start at 0 until real coordinates are collected) city : the city name for the location (text, up to 100 characters) zip_code : the zip code for the location (text, up to 50 characters) Together these columns are what let a member's account store each service area as a real geographic region: the bounding box records how far the area stretches on the map, and the city and zip code fields record what the area is called. That structure is what allows one member profile to represent coverage of several distinct cities or zip codes rather than one street address. Before this update, a stored service area only carried a single latitude and longitude point plus a text address. The installer also includes a second database step that verifies the four bounding-box coordinate columns exist. It makes no changes of its own; once the first step has added the columns, it reports success and clears. No existing data is modified or deleted. The update only adds columns, so every service area the site's members have already saved keeps all of its current values. Why It Appears It appears when the service_areas table on the website is missing one or more of the six columns listed above. This is a legacy condition: sites created before the Multi-Location Add-on stored bounding boxes, city names, and zip codes still have the older, smaller table layout, while newer sites already include these columns and never see this installer. Seeing this entry does not mean anything is broken. Why It Matters The Multi-Location Add-on's location tools read and write these columns when members manage their service areas. With the columns in place, each area a member selects can be saved with its full map boundary and its city or zip code. Without them, features that try to save this richer location data have nowhere to put it. This is a structural update: running it changes nothing visible on the website by itself, it makes the database ready for the features that use it. If Multi-Location Add-on does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running Nothing changes on the visitor-facing side of the website, and no member data needs review. The new columns start out empty (or 0 for the coordinates) on existing records and are filled in as members save areas going forward. If the site's members already have saved service areas, a separate installer named Migrate City - Zip Code Service Areas may appear in the same module afterward; it fills in the missing city and zip code values on those older records, and it requires the columns added here before it can run. After Running There is nothing visible to check on the front end, since the change is purely a database table. Once it has run, comment features backed by the Community Post Add-On have the storage they need, including support for holding comments in a waiting-for-approval state. The installer is safe to run at any time: it only creates a missing table or adds missing columns, and it leaves any existing comments untouched. results.title: Install Billing Reminder Email Settings - Dashboard Installer | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Install Billing Reminder Email Settings - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109033 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What Install Billing Reminder Email Settings Does This installer sets up the configuration the site needs for automated billing reminder emails. It creates the database table that stores the reminder rules (if the site does not have it yet) and then fills in the platform’s standard set of rules. It only adds what is missing, so nothing already present is changed or removed. Creates the email_automation_settings table in the site’s database if it does not already exist. Copies the platform’s standard billing reminder rules into that table. Each rule defines how many days from the related billing event the email is sent, whether the email goes to the member, whether a copy goes to the site admin, and whether a PDF attachment is included. Skips any rule that already exists in the table (matched by rule name), so rules that have already been customized keep their current settings. No rows are deleted or overwritten. Why It Appears The site is missing part of this configuration. Either the email_automation_settings table does not exist in the site’s database at all, which is common on older sites created before this feature was added, or the table exists but one or more of the platform’s standard rules are missing from it. The status check compares the table against the platform’s master list of rules, rule by rule, and the installer appears if any rule is absent. Why It Matters Billing reminder emails rely on these stored rules to know when to send, who to notify, and whether to attach a PDF. Until the rules are installed, that configuration does not exist on the site. Running the installer puts the standard rules in place with the platform’s default values. The installation does not send any emails by itself; it only installs the settings, which can be reviewed and adjusted in the admin area afterward. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, Install Billing Reminder Email Settings appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again — the entry disappears once all steps are done. If Install Billing Reminder Email Settings does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running A confirmation message appears that reads “Billing Automation Settings Add-on Installed”. Nothing changes on the live website, and no emails are sent as part of the installation. The new rules are stored with the platform’s default values, so this is a good time to review the billing reminder email settings in the admin area and adjust the timing, recipients, and PDF attachment option for each rule. The installer is safe to run on any site: it only adds missing data and never edits or deletes existing rules. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: API Updates - Dashboard Installer | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: API Updates - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109034 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What API Updates Does This installer makes one small maintenance change to the database table the site uses to log API activity. It updates the column that stores each API call’s response so it matches the platform’s current definition, which can hold long response text and the full range of Unicode characters. Specifically, it changes the api_response column in the bd_api_logs table to the TEXT data type with utf8mb4 encoding. No data is deleted, no other tables are touched, and nothing on the live website changes. Why It Appears It appears when the site’s database has the bd_api_logs table but its api_response column still uses a data type other than TEXT, which means the table was created under an older definition. This is a legacy condition: sites whose API log table was created after the current definition shipped already have the correct column type. If the site does not have the bd_api_logs table at all, there is nothing to update and the installer stays hidden. Why It Matters The bd_api_logs table records the responses returned by API calls made to the site, which is useful when troubleshooting an API integration. A column with an older, more limited data type can cut off long responses or mishandle special characters, leaving incomplete log entries. After this update the column can store the full response text, including 4-byte Unicode characters such as emoji. This is a minor consistency fix: it improves the reliability of the site’s API logs and has no effect on how the website looks or behaves for visitors. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, API Updates appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again — the entry disappears once all steps are done. If API Updates does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running A success message confirms the column was changed. There is nothing visible to verify on the website, because the change affects only how one internal logging column stores data. Existing log entries remain in place, and if the API is used, new log entries will record response text under the updated column definition. The change is a safe, one-time adjustment to a column definition and does not remove any data. results.title: Changelog - June 2026 | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Changelog - June 2026 Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109066 New Features: Released over 300 new color sets to choose from in Design Settings in the Admin , now sorted by color tags. The logo generator will also take into account the site's color set when generating a logo. Added a new date format option that displays dates in the YYYY-MM-DD format in the website's date and time format setting on the General Setting page in the Admin . Added new date format options that use a period as the separator (for example, dd.mm.yyyy) to the global date settings in the Admin, supporting regions that use this format. Released new API endpoints that return the full member category tree for a directory — including top, sub, and sub-sub categories — with an option to include the number of members in each category. In addition, the system now supports safely deleting a category through the API, with a safeguard that first reports how many members and subcategories would be affected before allowing a full removal. Released BD Butler PRO , an upgraded version of the BD Butler AI assistant that adds purchasable AI credits with automatic refills, saved chat history, and support for multiple separate conversations. Made the BD Butler AI assistant available on the Member Search and Transaction History pages in the Admin, allowing Admins to ask about member and revenue insights directly from those pages. Added the ability for Admins to filter reviews that are not associated with any member, along with the option to re-associate each of these reviews with an existing member or delete them on the Member Reviews page in the Admin . Released Kazakh as a new supported language, including full translations for website labels and email templates. Enhancements / Fixes: Added the ability to delete all member categories at once from the Admin, with a confirmation warning before the categories are permanently removed. Updated the Froala Editor to the latest version, improving stability and editing features across the Admin and frontend. Updated the Get User API endpoint so the password, token, and cookie fields are no longer included in API responses, improving data security. Updated the Universal Search Cache API and its documentation in the Admin to reflect only the endpoints that are currently available. Fixed an issue that caused event dates to display incorrectly on the frontend for events dated before 1970. Fixed an issue that caused the post author selector to freeze when choosing an author in the Admin Post Wizard on sites with a large number of members. Fixed an issue that caused API requests to be rejected with an authentication error when the API key header was sent in uppercase, affecting integrations such as Zapier on certain sites. Fixed an issue that caused custom "required" field settings on the search form to be ignored when submitting the form in some cases. Fixed an issue that caused 301 redirects to be ignored when the redirect URL contained the word "images". Fixed an issue that prevented the stock image importer from working correctly when the " Convert Uploaded Images to WebP " setting was enabled. Fixed an issue that caused a member's subscription to remain in a Pending status after a successful upgrade payment in some cases. Fixed an issue that caused members signing in with Google to be redirected to their Member Dashboard page instead of back to the review form, when the review form was restricted to members only. Fixed an issue that caused location searches on the Match Leads page in the Admin to return no results because the searched city was incorrectly replaced with the country name. Released an optional API permission that allows a member's login token to be returned by the API for custom integrations. This option is turned off by default and must be enabled per API key. Improved the Site Transfer Wizard in the Admin to make moving a website to a new server easier, including cPanel support and a smoother Cloudflare connection process. Enhanced the server transfer process in the Admin to automatically detect how a website's domain is pointed (CNAME or A record) and adjust the guided steps accordingly, reducing friction when moving a site to a new server. Improved the billing experience so that when a subscription is cancelled, the plan no longer shows a next billing date and the related actions (ending, pausing, or buying boosts) are correctly disabled. Additionally, the proration amount and date shown when reactivating a plan were corrected. Fixed an issue that allowed account forms to be saved while bypassing required fields in some cases. Required fields are now properly enforced before a form can be submitted. Fixed an issue that caused empty member search result pages to be treated as valid, indexable pages by search engines instead of returning a 404 error, which could cause search engines to crawl empty / thin pages. Fixed an issue that caused the help chat bubble to move out of place when scrolling on the Form Manager page in the Admin. It now stays anchored to the bottom corner of the screen. Fixed an issue that caused the Compose Email window in the Admin to close completely when selecting an image from the file manager, instead of inserting the selected image into the email. Fixed an issue that caused GIF downloads from the Stock Photos library (GIPHY) to time out when inserting them through the content editor in the Admin. GIFs now import quickly as animated images. Fixed an issue that caused the events listing and search pages to display an incorrect starting number in the "Showing X - Y of Z Results" label (showing 0 instead of 1) in some cases. Fixed an issue that caused the Bookmark "Saves" counter to be visible to logged-out visitors on member profile and post pages. The counter now only appears for logged-in members. Released a security update to the Membership Plan upgrade logic. Members can no longer switch to a membership plan that is set as non-searchable and has sign-ups disabled. Improved the BD Butler experience when editing Web Pages, Email Templates , and Newsletters in the Admin by moving the BD Butler button directly into the content editor's toolbar. Along with this, the separate "Upload Images" button was removed to streamline the toolbar. Added activity tracking for the Media Manager in the Admin, so the system now records when images are uploaded or deleted, along with which Admin performed each action. Improved the image optimization process for profile logo and cover image uploads in the Member Dashboard, bringing them in line with the optimization already applied to profile images for faster loading and better quality. Updated the getSiteInfo API endpoint to include the site's checkout page URL slug, making it easier to retrieve directly from the API. Fixed an issue that caused the system to remove saved revision history for widgets, page templates, content blocks, and SEO pages when saving changes, so the "Load Revision" option could lose previous versions in some cases. Fixed an issue that caused the previous and next page links in blog and search result pagination to include extra, malformed web address information in some cases. Fixed an issue that prevented embedded videos, such as Vimeo and YouTube, from expanding to the full width of their container on post detail pages, causing them to display at a small fixed size. Fixed an issue that caused the "Scroll to Message Field" button in Private Member Chat to position the top of the message box behind the site's fixed header, hiding part of the text field. Fixed an issue that caused deleting a category through the API to leave behind orphaned category associations instead of fully removing them. Fixed an issue that caused the Business Data Tool to create a new category even when that option had not been selected. Updated the in-app purchase experience that lets users complete a purchase directly in the Admin area. In addition, the system now prevents add-ons from being installed on top of the new plans which no longer use separate add-ons. Improved the loading speed of hero images on single post detail pages. Improved Membership Plan cloning in the Admin so that all plan data and settings are copied correctly, with appropriate default values applied to prevent missing settings when a plan is saved. Updated the Google Maps JS Delivery Optimization setting in the Admin so that, when required code is missing, the system now shows separate messages — one for the widgets that need to be disabled and another for the post settings that need to be changed back to their default values — making it clearer what needs to be addressed before enabling the setting. Fixed an issue in the Menu Manager that could prevent Admins from adding, editing, or deleting menu items in some cases. The system now validates each field and displays a clear error message below the field when an invalid character is entered. Fixed an issue that caused the system to remove the "+" character from the page title and social sharing title on member profile pages when a company name contained that character. Fixed an issue in the list_services API endpoint that allowed creating a service with an empty name or a duplicate entry. Fixed an issue that allowed members to publish a paid post through the Member Dashboard quick links without being prompted for the required payment, even though the same post correctly required payment when published from the sidebar. F ixed an issue that allowed a form to be saved while required fields were left empty in some cases. Fixed an issue that caused review images to appear broken when saved in .webp format. Fixed an issue that caused an image selected from the stock image library to be inserted at the bottom of the page instead of at the cursor position within the Froala Editor. Fixed an issue that caused the categories export file to be incomplete when exporting Member Categories in the Admin . Fixed an issue that caused custom content from a specific static page not to display on certain search results URLs, because the system was prioritizing a more general page. The system now correctly prioritizes the most specific static page. Fixed an issue that caused the in-app checkout window to appear over the Send Newsletter email preview in the Admin , when it should have remained hidden. Fixed an issue that prevented webhooks from being triggered when invoices and subscriptions were created through the Quick Create wizard , so they now fire the same webhooks as records created directly. Fixed an issue that caused blank member profiles to be created when importing members with missing required fields in the Admin . The import now stops and clearly identifies the rows that need correction. Fixed an issue that prevented newsletters from being created in the Admin on some websites. In all, over 60 feature enhancements and software updates were released this month. results.title: How to Cancel a Brilliant Directories Subscription | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How to Cancel a Brilliant Directories Subscription Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109071 Active Brilliant Directories subscriptions can be managed from the account management area, including the option to cancel a subscription when needed. This article explains how to access the cancellation option, review important account and billing details, and complete the cancellation process for an active subscription. For a full overview of the Account Dashboard, see this article: Account Dashboard Access Payments Subscription details are managed from the Brilliant Directories Account Dashboard. From the top navigation menu, click Payments . Select Website Plans from the dropdown menu. The Payments menu also includes access to: Billing History Payment Methods Website Plans Tab The Website Plans tab displays the active subscription details for each website connected to the account. Each website plan card can include: Website name Site ID Website status Current plan name Monthly or yearly subscription amount Next billing date Change Plan button Extra Resources button Three-dot menu with additional options Expandable usage details If multiple websites are connected to the same account, confirm the correct website name and Site ID before making any plan, billing, subscription, or cancellation changes. Change Plan The Change Plan button opens the available plan options for the selected website. Go to the Website Plans tab. Locate the website that needs to be updated. Click Change Plan . Review the available plan options. Select the preferred plan option when ready to make a change. The Change Plan screen displays the current plan, available plan options, plan pricing, and usage comparisons. Plan changes may apply immediately and may include prorated billing depending on the selected change. Extra Resources The Extra Resources button opens the resource management window for the selected website. Extra resources can include: Extra members Extra emails Extra bandwidth Extra storage The Extra Resources window displays the base amount included with the plan, current usage, available adjustment controls, and the updated monthly total before continuing. Go to the Website Plans tab. Locate the website that needs additional resources. Click Extra Resources . Adjust the available resource options as needed. Review the current total, adjustment amount, and new total. Click Continue to proceed. View Website Usage Details The arrow button on the website plan card expands the usage details for the selected website. Go to the Website Plans tab. Locate the website plan card. Click the arrow icon on the right side of the card. Review the usage details displayed below the plan card. When expanded, the website plan card can show usage information for: Members Emails AI Credits Bandwidth Storage Additional Website Plan Options The three-dot menu on the website plan card includes additional actions for the selected website. The available options include: Change Plan: Opens the plan selection screen. Pause Subscription: Opens the subscription pause flow. Delete Website: Opens the website cancellation flow. Important: Pausing a subscription and deleting a website are separate actions. The Delete Website option starts the cancellation process for the selected website subscription. Pause a Subscription The Pause Subscription option is available from the three-dot menu on the website plan card. Go to the Website Plans tab. Locate the website subscription that needs to be paused. Click the three-dot menu on the right side of the website plan card. Select Pause Subscription . Before You Go Screen for Pausing After selecting Pause Subscription , a Before You Go window may appear. This screen includes an option to contact the support team before continuing with the pause request. The available options include: Contact Support: Opens the support option for help with the account or website. Never Mind: Closes the pause flow and keeps the subscription active. I Still Want to Pause: Continues to the subscription pause options. Choose When the Pause Takes Effect The Pause Subscription window allows the account owner to choose when the pause should take effect. The available pause options are: At the end of the billing cycle: The website stays online until the listed billing date. No future charges are made after the paid billing cycle ends. Pause immediately: The website goes offline immediately. Email and connections stop working immediately. The selected option controls when the subscription pause takes effect. What Happens When a Subscription Is Paused The Pause Subscription window explains what happens when a website subscription is paused. Billing stops and the account will not be charged at the next cycle. Add-ons and extra resources pause alongside the subscription. Website data and settings are preserved. The subscription can be reactivated later. A prorated charge may apply if the subscription is reactivated after the paid cycle has ended. Review these details carefully before confirming the pause request. Cancel a Website Subscription The Delete Website option opens the cancellation flow for the selected website subscription. Go to the Website Plans tab. Locate the website subscription that needs to be canceled. Click the three-dot menu on the right side of the website plan card. Select Delete Website . A confirmation window will open before the cancellation options are shown. Confirm the correct website name is displayed before continuing. Before You Cancel Screen After selecting Delete Website , a We’d Love to Keep You window may appear. This screen provides alternatives before continuing with the cancellation request. The available options include: Pause Subscription: Opens the pause subscription option instead of canceling. Contact Support: Opens the support option for help with the account or website. Never Mind: Closes the cancellation flow and keeps the subscription active. I Still Want to Cancel: Continues to the cancellation confirmation screen. Choose When the Cancellation Takes Effect The Cancel Subscription window allows the account owner to choose when the cancellation should take effect. The available cancellation options are: At the end of the billing cycle: The website stays online until the listed billing date. No future charges are made after the paid billing cycle ends. Immediately: The website goes offline immediately. Email and all connections stop working immediately. The selected option controls when the cancellation takes effect. What Happens When a Subscription Is Canceled The Cancel Subscription window explains what happens when a website subscription is canceled. The subscription is marked Cancelled and the website will be suspended. All add-ons and extra resources are canceled alongside the subscription. After 30 days of suspension, the website is archived for long-term backup storage. The website subscription can be reactivated within the 30-day window. Review these details carefully before confirming the cancellation request. Confirm the Cancellation The cancellation form requires a reason for cancellation and a typed confirmation before the final cancellation button becomes available. Select when the cancellation should take effect. Review the details in the What cancellation does section. Enter the reason for cancellation in the available field. Type CANCEL in the confirmation field. Click the final cancellation button. The final confirmation button may show: Cancel at End of Cycle Cancel Now The subscription is not canceled until the final cancellation button is clicked. Click Keep Subscription to exit the cancellation flow and keep the subscription active. Billing History Tab The Billing History tab displays invoices connected to the account. Invoice records can include: Invoice date Description Website name and Site ID Status Amount View invoice option Download invoice option Search and Filter Billing History The Billing History tab includes tools to search and filter invoice records. Available billing history filters include: Search invoices: Search billing records by invoice-related details. All Sites: Filter invoices by website. All Status: Filter invoices by invoice status. The website filter can be used to view invoices for all websites or a specific website connected to the account. The status filter can include: All Status Paid Past Due Failed Refunded View Invoice Details The eye icon opens the invoice details window for the selected invoice. Go to the Billing History tab. Locate the invoice that needs to be reviewed. Click the eye icon on the right side of the invoice row. The Invoice Details window can include: Invoice number Due date Description Status Payment method Total due Download option Download an Invoice Invoices can be downloaded from the Billing History tab or from the Invoice Details window. Go to the Billing History tab. Locate the invoice that needs to be downloaded. Click the download icon on the right side of the invoice row. A PDF copy of the invoice will open or download depending on the browser settings. Payment Methods Tab The Payment Methods tab displays saved payment methods connected to the account. This area can be used to: View the primary payment method See which payment method is used for subscriptions Add a new payment method Remove an existing card when available The payment method card displays limited card details, such as the card brand, last four digits, and expiration date. Payment information is encrypted and securely stored. Full card numbers are not stored in the Brilliant Directories account area. Add a Payment Method A new payment method can be added from the Payment Methods tab. Go to the Payment Methods tab. Click Add Payment Method . Enter the card number. Enter the expiration date. Enter the security code. Select the billing country. Click Save Payment Method . The Add a Payment Method window may accept card details, PayPal, or other payment methods enabled on the account. Payment details are sent directly to Stripe for processing. Remove a Payment Method An existing payment method can be removed from the Payment Methods tab when the remove option is available. Go to the Payment Methods tab. Locate the saved payment method. Click the three-dot menu on the payment method card. Select Remove . If a payment method is being used for active subscriptions, another valid payment method may need to be added before the existing one can be removed. Important Notes Always confirm the correct website name and Site ID before changing a plan, adding resources, pausing a subscription, canceling a subscription, or reviewing invoices. Pausing a subscription stops future billing based on the selected pause option. Pausing immediately takes the website offline right away. Pausing at the end of the billing cycle keeps the website online through the paid billing period. Add-ons and extra resources pause with the subscription when a subscription is paused. Canceling a subscription marks the subscription as cancelled and the website will be suspended. Add-ons and extra resources are canceled alongside the subscription when a subscription is canceled. After 30 days of suspension, a canceled website is archived for long-term backup storage. A canceled website subscription can be reactivated within the 30-day window. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: Install Admin Reviews Support - Dashboard Installer | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Install Admin Reviews Support - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109078 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What Install Admin Reviews Support Does This installer prepares the database and review form so the site can use the newer member reviews module. It runs six steps that add a tracking column, wire up the ratings field, tidy the admin review layout, and label the existing reviews so they belong to the new form. It changes structure and settings, it does not delete the reviews. The six steps do the following: Review form tag column : adds a formname column (varchar) to the users_reviews table so each review can record which form it came from. Overall rating field : if the site has a customized member_review form, it adds a rating_overall field to the form_fields table for that form, backed by the [widget=Bootstrap Theme - Admin - Return Overall Rating] widget, and shifts the other fields down one position to make room. If the site is still using the platform master review form, this step is skipped. Hide the write-a-review label in admin : for the field at position 2 on the member_review form, it turns off the email, search, and grid views so that label stops showing inside the admin reviews module. Hide the rating options in admin : for the [widget=Bootstrap Theme - Form - Display Rating Options] field (field type Custom), it turns off the email, search, and grid views so the rating options are hidden in the admin reviews module. Migrate existing reviews : any row in users_reviews that has no formname value is set to member_review , so the existing reviews are attached to the new form. Ratings field name update : renames the field_name of the display rating options field to ratings in the form_fields table. Why It Appears The installer runs six status checks against the database and form configuration, and it appears whenever at least one of them still has work to do. In plain terms, it shows up when the formname column is missing from users_reviews , when a customized member_review form is missing the rating_overall field, when the write-a-review label or the rating options are still visible in the admin reviews module, when the site has reviews whose formname is empty, or when the display rating options field has not yet been renamed to ratings . These are legacy conditions from before the newer reviews module became standard. Seeing the installer does not mean anything is broken, it means the review setup predates one or more of these updates. Why It Matters Running the installer lets the site use the newer member reviews module the way it is designed to work: reviews are tagged to the right form, the overall rating field is in place, and the admin reviews module is not cluttered by fields meant only for the front end. The reviews migration is the practical piece, it labels the existing reviews so they continue to appear under the new form instead of being left untagged. Skipping the installer leaves the reviews on the older structure, and features built for the new module may not behave as expected. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, Install Admin Reviews Support appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again. The entry disappears once all steps are done. If Install Admin Reviews Support does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date. The module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. The data_flows table (which stores the lead flows), the data_flow_actions table (which stores the settings for each flow, EG which email templates and auto-match options a flow uses), and the form_inquiries table (which stores contact-form inquiries). Each table is created only if it does not already exist. Seeds a default flow and default action. If no flow named default_flow exists, it inserts one into data_flows . If no main action exists (a row in data_flow_actions marked main_flow_action = 1), it inserts a "Main Action" record with the standard template and auto-match defaults. Cleans up the leads table. It removes a set of unused legacy columns from the leads table (EG lead_address , lead_city , lead_state , lead_zip , lead_source , and others). Each column is dropped only if it holds no data, so populated columns are left untouched. Adds the newer lead columns. It adds any missing columns that the current Lead System uses to the leads table, including lead_message , top_id , sub_id , the location fields lat , lng , swlat , swlng , nelat , nelng , location_type , lead_location , country_sn , and adm_lvl_1_sn , plus flow_source , formname , lead_notes , and origin_ip . Only columns that are not already present are added. Migrates older lead data. For leads whose details are still stored in the users_meta table, it copies those values into the matching columns on the leads table (in batches of 2,000) and then removes the migrated rows from users_meta . Adds a form column. It adds the form_action_type column to the forms table if that column is missing. Fixes lead match statuses. It adds the lead_status_was_update column to the lead_matches table if missing, then remaps older lead_status values to their current equivalents for leads that use the new format, marking each row it updates so it is not touched again. Updates the search engine reference. On any flow still set to the old value "Get Matched Search Engine", it updates the search_engine field in data_flows to the current value "Search - Member - Search Query". Turns the Lead System on. It sets the enable_data_flows setting in website_settings to 1 (the Basic Package), creating the setting if it does not exist, and sets the enable_member_search_and_lead_matching_system setting to 1 so the current member-search and lead-matching widgets are active. Standardizes the contact form email field. If the site uses a customized contact_form whose email field is named email , it renames that field to inquiry_email in form_fields so inquiries are captured correctly. Sites using the master contact form are left as-is. Offers a cache refresh as the final step. Seeing it does not mean anything is broken. It means the database predates one or more of these Lead System updates. Why It Matters Running the installer puts the Lead System on the current structure the platform expects: the tables, columns, default flow, and settings that inquiry capture and lead matching rely on. It also moves older lead details into the current lead columns so that data displays and behaves consistently. Skipping it will not delete anything, but the Lead System features may not work as intended on the older structure, and older lead data may stay in a place newer screens do not read from. After it completes, click Check For Updates again. The entry disappears once all steps are done. If Update Lead System does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date. The module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running Nothing changes visibly on the website. The updates are internal: the leads, inquiries, and forms keep their existing data, older lead details are moved into the current lead columns rather than discarded, and the Lead System settings are switched on. What Install User Consent Tools (GDPR) Does This installer adds GDPR consent capture to the website. It does two things: it adds database columns so consent can be recorded with each record, and it adds a consent checkbox field to the public-facing forms. It changes database structure and form layout; it does not delete or rewrite the existing content. First, it adds a user_consent column (a TEXT field) to five database tables, one step per table, if the column is not already there: users_data (member listings) users_reviews (member reviews) contacts (contact submissions) leads (leads) form_inquiries (form inquiries) Second, it inserts a consent checkbox field into the forms. The field is named user_consent_gdpr , is a Custom field type, is added as not required, and displays a consent-checkboxes widget. It is added only to forms that already exist on the site, and only if that form does not already have the field. The forms and the widget each one uses are: whmcs_signup_paid , signup_free , and whmcs_signup_external (paid, free, and external signup forms) use the Bootstrap Theme - Form - User Consent Checkboxes widget. whmcs_upgrade_account (the account upgrade form) uses the Bootstrap Theme - Form - User Consent Checkboxes widget. member_review (the member review form) uses the Bootstrap Theme - Form - Review Consent Checkboxes widget. contact_form (the contact us form) uses the Bootstrap Theme - Form - Contact Form Consent Checkboxes widget. bootstrap_get_match (the lead form) uses the Bootstrap Theme - Form - Lead Consent Checkboxes widget. newsletter_signup_footer and newsletter_signup (the footer and standard newsletter forms) use the Bootstrap Theme - Form - Newsletter Consent Checkboxes widget. On the signup and lead forms, if the installer finds an existing terms-and-conditions link field, it hides that field and places the new consent field in the same position. Otherwise it places the consent field just before the form's reCAPTCHA. On the other forms the consent field is inserted next to the form's reCAPTCHA, save button, or honeypot field. Why It Appears This installer runs twelve separate checks and appears whenever at least one of them finds something still missing. For the five database steps, a step is pending if its table does not yet have a user_consent column. For the form steps, a step is pending only when that form already exists on the site and does not yet contain the user_consent_gdpr field. If a form is not present on the site, that step reports the form is not customized and offers no action. In plain terms, it shows up when any of the five consent columns is missing, or when any of the existing forms is missing its consent checkbox. Sites that already have every column and every form field in place will not see this installer. Why It Matters GDPR compliance depends on both recording consent and asking for it. The user_consent columns give each member listing, review, contact, lead, and form inquiry a place to store the consent captured at submission time. The consent checkbox fields put an explicit opt-in on the signup, upgrade, review, contact, lead, and newsletter forms, so visitors actively agree before submitting. Skipping the installer will not break the current site, but the forms will not present a consent checkbox and there will be no column to store consent against these records. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, Install User Consent Tools (GDPR) appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again. The entry disappears once all steps are done. If Install User Consent Tools (GDPR) does not appear in the list, the website already has the consent columns and form fields in place, so there is nothing to do. After Running A consent checkbox appears on each affected form (signup, upgrade, review, contact, lead, and newsletter), and each of the five tables gains its user_consent column. The existing form fields and records keep their data. On the signup and lead forms, any previous terms-and-conditions field is hidden rather than deleted, replaced in place by the new consent field. Each step re-checks the database and forms before making any change. The column steps look for the user_consent column first, and the form steps look for the existing user_consent_gdpr field and report a warning instead of adding a duplicate. This makes the installer safe to run even if part of it was applied earlier. Because the form steps only touch forms that already exist, if one of these forms is added to the site later, run the installer again to add the consent field to it. The three steps do the following: Revision count column : adds a revision_count column (BIGINT, default 0) to both the data_posts table and the users_portfolio_groups table, placed after the state_sn column. This column counts how many times a post has been saved. Property square footage : changes the property_sqr_foot column on the users_portfolio_groups table to DECIMAL(10,2) that allows empty (NULL) values, so the field can be left blank. Property price : changes the property_price column on the users_portfolio_groups table to DECIMAL(20,2) that allows empty (NULL) values, so the field can be left blank. If the site does not have a property_price column at all, this step reports nothing to run and is skipped. Why It Appears The installer runs three status checks against the database structure and appears whenever at least one still has work to do. In plain terms, it shows up when revision_count is missing from either data_posts or users_portfolio_groups , when the property_sqr_foot column does not yet allow empty values, or when the property_price column does not yet allow empty values. These are legacy conditions. Databases created before these column updates became standard will see the installer offered. Seeing it does not mean anything is broken, it means the database predates one or more of these structure updates. Why It Matters The revision_count column gives the platform a place to track how many times a post has been saved, which post type features use. Allowing the property square footage and property price fields to hold empty values means members can leave those fields blank instead of being forced to enter a number, which matters for real estate style post types. Skipping the installer will not break the current site, but it leaves the database on the older structures that these features expect. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has pending steps, Revision Count - Post Types Update appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again. The entry disappears once all steps are done. If Revision Count - Post Types Update does not appear in the list, the website is already up to date. The module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running Nothing changes visibly on the website. The updates are internal database structure changes: the posts keep their existing data, the new revision_count column starts at 0, and the two property fields can now be saved empty. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward. The revision count step re-checks both tables before adding the column, and the two property field steps re-apply the same column definition, so the installer is safe to run even if part of the update was applied earlier. Click Check For Updates again and the entry disappears once all three checks pass. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Folder Permissions Security - Dashboard Installer | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Folder Permissions Security - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109104 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What Folder Permissions Security Does This installer is a filesystem cleanup, not a database change. It connects to the website's hosting account, scans the folders under the site's /public_html directory (the web root where the files live), and finds any folders whose permissions are not set to the secure standard. It then resets those folders to permission mode 0755 . It only adjusts folder permissions; it does not move, rename, or delete any files or folders, and it does not touch the content. In practical terms: The installer opens a connection to the hosting account using the site's stored hosting credentials. It walks the folders under /public_html and collects every folder that is not already at the correct permission. It sets each of those folders to 0755 — the standard secure permission for web directories, where the account owner can read, write, and open the folder, and everyone else can only read and open it. Why It Appears Each time Check For Updates is clicked, this installer connects to the hosting account and scans /public_html for folders that are not at the secure permission. It appears in the list only when that scan finds at least one folder that still needs adjusting. If every folder is already set correctly, the installer reports that everything is fine and does not offer anything to install. Folders can drift out of the secure setting for ordinary reasons — files uploaded through certain tools, restores, or migrations can leave folders with looser permissions than the platform standard. Seeing this installer does not mean the site has been tampered with; it means the scan found folders that are not yet locked down to the recommended setting. Why It Matters Folder permissions control who is allowed to read and change the files inside a directory on the server. Folders left with permissions looser than 0755 can be writable or accessible more broadly than they should be, which is a security weakness. Tightening every folder under the web root to the 0755 standard closes that gap and keeps the site's files under the correct level of protection. It is a security hardening step; it will not change how the website looks or behaves for visitors. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the site has folders that need adjusting, Folder Permissions Security appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again — the entry disappears once every folder is at the secure permission. If Folder Permissions Security does not appear in the list, the folders are already secured — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running Nothing changes visibly on the website. The files, folders, and content are all left exactly where they were; only the permission settings on the affected folders are tightened to 0755 . There is nothing to reconfigure afterward. The installer re-scans the folders every time it runs and only adjusts the ones that are still out of compliance, so it is safe to run again. Click Check For Updates after installing, and the entry disappears once the scan finds no remaining folders to fix. results.title: Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB - Dashboard Installer | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB - Dashboard Installer Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109105 The Install New Updates module on the admin dashboard lists one-time platform installers that still have pending steps on the site. Clicking the green Check For Updates button refreshes the list — an installer only appears when the site actually has something left to install, and it disappears from the list once its steps are complete. What Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB Does This installer modernizes how the website's database tables are stored. It finds any tables still using the older MyISAM storage engine and converts them to InnoDB , the modern engine that newer database versions and platform features expect. It changes the storage engine only; it does not delete, rewrite, or reorder the data inside the tables. How the conversion works: The installer connects to the website database and looks up every table still on the MyISAM engine. It converts them to InnoDB with a standard ALTER TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB operation, processing the smallest tables first . Each run works within a 45-second time budget . If there are large tables and the budget is reached before every table is done, the remaining tables are left for the next run. This is deliberate: it keeps large log tables from causing the request to time out. Two tables — website_layouts and website_layouts_old — are intentionally skipped. Their rows are too wide for InnoDB's row-size limit and cannot be converted without schema changes, so the installer leaves them on MyISAM by design. Why It Appears Each time Check For Updates is clicked, this installer counts the tables in the database that are still on the MyISAM engine (ignoring the two skipped layout tables). It appears in the list only when that count is greater than zero — that is, when at least one convertible table is still on MyISAM. Once every eligible table has been converted to InnoDB, the count is zero and the installer no longer appears. This is a legacy condition. Databases created before InnoDB became the platform standard will have MyISAM tables to convert, while newer databases are already on InnoDB throughout. Seeing this installer does not mean anything is broken; it means the database still has one or more tables on the older engine. Why It Matters InnoDB is the modern MySQL storage engine and the one newer database server versions and platform features are built for. It supports row-level locking and transactional integrity that MyISAM does not, which makes tables more reliable under concurrent activity and better protected against corruption. Converting the remaining MyISAM tables brings the database in line with the current standard. Leaving them on MyISAM will not break the current site, but it keeps those tables on an engine that newer features are not designed around. How to Run It From the admin dashboard, find the Install New Updates module and click Check For Updates . If the database still has MyISAM tables, Convert tables From MyISAM to INNODB appears in the list. Click Install . After it completes, click Check For Updates again — the entry disappears once every eligible table has been converted. If the installer does not appear in the list, the tables are already on InnoDB — the module only shows installers with pending steps, so there is nothing to do. After Running Nothing changes visibly on the website. The data in the tables is preserved exactly as it was; only the underlying storage engine is switched from MyISAM to InnoDB. There is nothing to reconfigure afterward. Because each run works within a time budget and processes tables smallest-first, a database with large tables may not finish in a single pass. When that happens, the installer reports how many tables still remain and stays in the list — simply run it again to continue where it left off. Each run re-checks which tables are still on MyISAM before converting, so it is safe to run repeatedly until none remain and the entry disappears. results.title: BD Butler: Scheduled AI Tasks, Skills and Routines | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: BD Butler: Scheduled AI Tasks, Skills and Routines Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109264 BD Butler can create website content as a one-time task or automatically on a recurring schedule. Scheduled tasks run in the background through Brilliant Directories. The website admin does not need to remain open, and the computer does not need to stay turned on while a task is running. This article expands on the main BD Butler article and covers the Tasks, Skills, and Routines available inside BD Butler PRO. [Read] BD Butler [WATCH] AI Website Automation: Schedule Content Creation [WATCH] Scheduled AI Tasks: Create Website Content While You Sleep Understanding Skills, Tasks and Routines BD Butler uses three connected components: Skill: A predefined job BD Butler knows how to complete, such as creating a blog article, event, or job listing. Routine: A saved Task that runs repeatedly according to a selected schedule. Task: A single execution of a selected Skill. For example, the Create a Job Listing Skill can be run once as a Task or saved as a Routine that searches for and creates new job listings every week. Available Skills The following 3 built-in Skills are currently available. Create a Blog Article Researches a topic related to the website and creates an article that can include: SEO-focused written content An article image Internal links to related website content Links to relevant external sources Post and SEO details Create an Event Post Searches for a real upcoming event and creates an event post using information from the event’s official source. The instructions can focus the search by: Location Industry Event type Audience Date range Create a Job Listing Searches for an active job opportunity and creates a formatted job listing. The instructions can focus the search by: Job title Industry Location Experience level Employer type When information is available, the generated listing can also include compensation details and a link to the employer’s official job page. Create a New Task Click the New Task tab. Select the Skill to run: Blog, Event, Job Enter a nickname for the Task. Add Custom Instructions Custom instructions tell BD Butler what type of content to create. This field is optional. Without additional instructions, BD Butler can review the website name, URL, menus, categories, footer links, and recent content to determine a relevant topic. Adding instructions provides greater control over the results. Blog Article Example Create articles about preparing for a first half marathon. Cover training plans, recovery, nutrition, and choosing a running coach. Event Post Example Find upcoming small-business networking events in Austin, Texas. Only include events with an official registration page. Job Listing Example Find active remote marketing manager positions at software companies in the United States. Instructions can also define the preferred structure, including: Article length Sections to include Locations to target Topics to avoid Preferred audience Whether FAQs or bullet points should be included Internal or external linking preferences For recurring Routines, use instructions broad enough to produce different results during future runs while remaining focused on the same subject. Choose the Number of Posts Select how many items BD Butler should create during each run. Available quantities include: 1 post (2 credits) 2 posts (4 credits) 3 posts (6 credits) A maximum of three posts can be created during one Task. Keeping each run within this limit helps maintain consistent research and content quality. For a Routine, the selected quantity will be created each time the Routine runs. For example, a weekly Routine set to create three blog articles will attempt to create three new articles during every weekly run. Choose Draft or Published Status Select how the generated content should be saved. Publish Live The content is published automatically after the Task is completed successfully. Before using this option with a recurring Routine, run the Task at least once in draft mode and review the results. Save as Draft The content is created but does not appear publicly until it is reviewed and published manually. Draft mode is recommended when testing a new Skill, prompt, or recurring Routine. Choose the Post Author Select the member or admin account that will be assigned as the author of the generated content. The selected author will appear as the content owner when the post is created. One author can be selected for each Task or Routine. Schedule the Task A Task can run once or be placed on a recurring schedule. Run Once Now Runs the Task one time immediately. This option is useful for: Testing new instructions Reviewing the type of content produced Creating a single article, event, or job listing Confirming the selected author and post status Hourly Runs the Task approximately once every hour. Daily Runs the Task approximately once each day. Weekly Runs the Task on selected days of the week. Different Routines can be assigned to different days. For example: Monday: Industry blog articles Wednesday: Upcoming events Friday: New job listings Scheduled Tasks may run up to approximately 15 minutes before or after the selected time. This built-in offset helps distribute scheduled processing and means a Routine may not always begin at the exact minute shown. Set the Number of Runs Recurring Routines can continue until they are manually stopped or can be limited to a specific number of runs. A run limit can be useful for short content campaigns. Once the selected number of runs has been completed, the Routine stops automatically. Manage Existing Routines Saved Routines can be managed from the Routines list. Available actions can include: Start or stop a Routine Edit the Routine settings Run the Routine manually Clone the Routine Review previous runs Edit a Routine Editing a Routine changes the settings used during its next run. This can be used to update: Custom instructions Content quantity Author Publishing status Schedule Run limit Previously completed Tasks and content are not changed. Clone a Routine Cloning creates a copy that can be adjusted without changing the original Routine. For example, an existing job listing Routine can be cloned to target a different city, job title, or experience level. Run a Routine Manually A saved Routine can be run manually without waiting for its next scheduled time. This creates an additional Task using the Routine’s current settings. Completed The Completed tab provides a history of AI Tasks that are finished, currently processing, or were stopped before completion. Each task card can display: The task nickname The selected Skill Whether it was a manual or scheduled run The date and time it started The processing time The number of credits used The admin account that initiated the task The current task status Although the tab is labeled Completed , it also includes tasks that are still running or were stopped. Filter the Task List Use the available filters to locate a specific task. The status dropdown includes: Any Status Done Running Stopped Enter a task nickname in the Filter by name field to narrow the results further. Click Refresh to check for updated task statuses. Running Tasks A task that is still processing displays a blue Running status. Running tasks include a Stop button that can be used to cancel the task before it finishes. The BD Butler window and browser do not need to remain open while a task is processing. Return to the Completed tab later and click Refresh to check its progress. Completed Tasks A successfully completed task displays a green Done status. Completed task cards can also show: How long the task took to complete How many credits were used A Re-Run button An arrow for opening additional task details and results Use Re-Run to repeat the task using the same configuration. Stopped Tasks A canceled task displays a red Stopped status. The task card includes a message confirming that the task was canceled. When applicable, it will also confirm that no credits were used. Stopped tasks can be run again by clicking Re-Run . For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Create Custom Checkout And Sign Up Forms | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Create Custom Checkout And Sign Up Forms Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109267 This article explains how to assign a custom signup or checkout form to each membership plan. Edit Checkout Pages: Overview This feature allows different membership plans to collect different information during signup. For example, a free member plan can use a short basic signup form, while a paid professional plan can collect additional business, billing, or profile details during checkout. Overview By default, websites include signup forms for different membership signup and checkout flows. These forms control which fields display when a new member signs up for a membership plan. There are three default signup forms available: Member - Sign Up - Free Member - Sign Up - Paid Member - Sign Up - External Payment Each form is designed for a specific type of membership plan or checkout flow. Difference Between On-Site and Off-Site Payment Gateways Form Name Shortcode Used For Member - Sign Up - Free [form=signup_free] Free membership plans Member - Sign Up - Paid [form=whmcs_signup_paid] Paid membership plans using onsite checkout Member - Sign Up - External Payment [form=whmcs_signup_external] Paid membership plans using an * off-site payment gateway, such as PayPal Step 1: Clone the Signup Form Start by cloning the existing signup form that matches the type of membership plan being customized. How To Clone a Form Clone Member - Sign Up - Free for a free membership plan. Clone Member - Sign Up - Paid for a paid membership plan using onsite checkout. Clone Member - Sign Up - External Payment for a paid membership plan using an * off-site payment gateway . The cloned form will include the required signup fields and system settings from the original form. Step 2: Rename the Cloned Form After cloning the form, rename it so it can be selected inside the membership plan settings. The form name must start with: Member - Sign Up Naming examples: Member - Sign Up - Free - Basic Plan Member - Sign Up - Free - Community Plan Member - Sign Up - Paid - Professional Plan Member - Sign Up - Paid - Business Plan Member - Sign Up - External Payment - Sponsor Plan Use a clear name that identifies which membership plan the form is intended for. If the form name does not start with Member - Sign Up , it will not appear as an option in the membership plan signup form setting. Step 3: Customize the Form Fields After the form has been cloned and renamed, edit the form fields as needed. How To Customize a Form Fields can be added, removed, renamed, reordered, or marked as required based on the information that should be collected during signup. When editing the form, keep the following in mind: Do not remove required system fields needed for signup or checkout. Do not remove payment fields from paid signup forms. Do not add payment fields to free signup forms. Do not change the checkout flow by using the wrong form type. Keep the form focused on the information needed at signup. Save the form after making changes. Important: If a required checkout or registration field is removed, the signup process may not work correctly. Step 4: Assign the Form to a Membership Plan After the custom signup form has been created, assign it to the membership plan. Go to Finance >> Membership Plans . Click Edit for the membership plan that needs a custom signup form. Use the admin search field at the top of the page and search for Sign Up Form . In the Sign Ups & Upgrades section, find the Sign Up Form setting. Select the signup form from the dropdown. The selected form will now be used when new members sign up for that membership plan. Note: For a form to appear as an option in the dropdown, the form name must start with Member - Sign Up . Keep Signup Forms Short for Better Conversions When customizing signup forms, it is best to keep the form as short and focused as possible. 5 Ways to Optimize Checkout Pages to Increase Membership Sign Ups Create a Signup Form That Works! Long checkout forms can reduce signup conversions because they create extra work before the user has completed registration. If a form feels too long, repetitive, or tedious, users may exit before finishing the signup process. A shorter form helps users complete signup faster and creates a smoother checkout experience. Recommended Signup Form Guidelines Only ask for information that is needed during signup. Move non-essential profile details to the member dashboard after signup. Avoid asking for the same information in multiple ways. Use clear field labels so members understand what to enter. Keep required fields limited to the most important information. Use optional fields for details that are helpful but not required. For example, a paid business plan may need the member’s name, email, company name, phone number, billing information, and payment details at checkout. However, details such as a full business description, social media links, extra images, certifications, or extended profile content can often be collected later from the member dashboard. Important Form Requirements Do not assign the free signup form to a paid membership plan. Paid plans need the correct paid or external payment form so the checkout process can work properly. Do not assign the onsite paid signup form to a free membership plan. Free plans do not require payment fields, and adding payment fields to a free signup can create confusion during the signup process. Do not assign the onsite paid signup form to a plan that uses an off-site payment gateway . Off-site payment plans need the external payment signup form so the off-site payment flow works as expected. Common Mistakes to Avoid Creating a new form from scratch: Clone the existing free, paid, or external payment signup form instead. Using the wrong form type: Free plans should use free signup forms. Paid plans should use the correct paid or external payment signup form. Using the wrong form name: The form name must start with Member - Sign Up . Making the form too long: Long forms can reduce completed signups. Removing required checkout fields: Removing required system fields can break registration or checkout. Not testing the signup flow: Always test the form after assigning it to a membership plan.
