results.title: How to Migrate a Domain Connection from A Record to CNAME | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How to Migrate a Domain Connection from A Record to CNAME Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109346 A CNAME connection uses the site's unique directoryup.com target instead of tying a hostname to a server IP. This allows the connection to follow the website when its hosting server changes. Before starting Have access to the DNS provider that currently hosts the domain's records. Record the existing values, confirm the website being connected, and preserve email and unrelated service records. This procedure changes DNS pointing; it does not require changing the website's domain name. Update www or another subdomain Open Settings > Domain Manager > Domain . Locate the site's connection details. Copy the unique directoryup.com target. Open the current DNS provider's record editor. Replace the conflicting address record for the intended hostname with a CNAME to the copied target. Save the change. Return to Domain Manager and click Check again . Type: CNAME Name: www, or the exact subdomain being connected Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target copied from Domain Manager Remove only the record that conflicts at that hostname. A CNAME cannot share its hostname with ordinary A/AAAA records or other data. Do not remove unrelated MX, TXT, or mailbox records. Handle the root domain separately The root domain is the address without a prefix, such as example.com . DNS does not allow an ordinary CNAME record on the root, so the right record depends on the company that runs the domain's DNS. Do not delete a working root record before its replacement is ready. Brilliant Directories nameservers: nothing to change; the records are managed for the website. Cloudflare: Cloudflare flattens a CNAME on the root, so the root takes the same CNAME as www, pointing to the site's unique target. GoDaddy: GoDaddy does not allow a CNAME on the root. When the website uses the www version, keep the www CNAME and turn on GoDaddy Domain Forwarding so example.com forwards to https://www.example.com with Permanent (301) . When the website uses the version without www, the root keeps an A record instead, and forwarding must stay off. Namecheap: replace the root record with an ALIAS record for @ pointing to the site's unique target. Namecheap does not allow an ALIAS alongside an existing A, AAAA, CNAME, or redirect record for the same host, so delete the current root record first. Other DNS providers: the root keeps an A record pointing to the server address shown in Domain Manager. An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. Moving the domain's DNS to a free Cloudflare account avoids this. Step-by-step instructions and the exact records for each case are in Point the root domain in the connection guide. Verify the result Confirm both the intended hostname and the root-domain behavior. The Domain tab can report separate results for each address. If Cloudflare proxying is enabled, a public DNS lookup may show Cloudflare addresses rather than the underlying CNAME; inspect the record in the connected Cloudflare DNS editor as well. Finally, open the website over HTTPS and confirm email still works. See DNS records in Domain Manager for the distinction between editable records and a public DNS view. results.title: Content » Web Page Builder » Draft System (Autosave) | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Content » Web Page Builder » Draft System (Autosave) Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109411 While editing a page in the Web Page Builder, the system automatically saves work in progress as a draft every few seconds. If the tab closes accidentally, the browser crashes, or the editor is closed before clicking Save, the changes aren't lost, the draft is offered back so editing can continue right where it left off. This article explains how the draft system works, what counts as a change, and how to discard one. How It Works As edits are made in the Web Page Builder, the system silently saves a draft copy of the page every 2 seconds. A status badge next to the Save button reflects the current state, for example: Saving Draft — the draft is being written Draft saved Just now — the latest changes are saved as a draft What Counts as a Change The draft system captures any edit made in the page editor, including: Typing or editing text (including single keystrokes, like adding a space) Rearranging or restyling content Inserting an image Inserting a video Changing Page Details and Page Options settings Any of these will trigger the autosave and update the draft badge. Drafts Don't Go Live Saving a draft is not the same as publishing. Nothing written to a draft ever appears on the live, front-facing page until Save is explicitly clicked on the page. This means edits can be made freely, experimenting, stepping away, or losing connection mid-edit, without any risk of half-finished changes showing up for site visitors. Clicking Save publishes the changes and clears the auto-saved draft, since it's no longer needed once the page is saved. Discarding a Draft To discard a draft, click the "Discard Draft" button. This deletes the draft and reverts the page back to its last saved (original) state. How to Disable This Functionality If needed, this functionality can be disabled under Settings » Advanced Settings by disabling the Auto-Save Drafts advanced setting. results.title: Brilliant Directories Mobile App: Manage Your Website From Anywhere | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Brilliant Directories Mobile App: Manage Your Website From Anywhere Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109533 The Brilliant Directories mobile app gives website admins a convenient way to monitor important website activity directly from an iPhone. View member information, revenue, form submissions, account activity, and website statistics without needing to log in to the full Admin Dashboard from a browser. The app is designed primarily for quick access and monitoring while away from a computer, making it easier to keep an eye on day-to-day website activity from one streamlined mobile dashboard. Download and Log In to the Brilliant Directories App The Brilliant Directories app can be downloaded from the Apple App Store by searching for Brilliant Directories . After installing the app, log in using the email address and password associated with a Brilliant Directories admin account. https://apps.apple.com/app/brilliant-directories/id898641614?l=en-GB On supported devices, the app can also use Face ID for faster sign-ins. When prompted, select whether to allow Brilliant Directories to use Face ID. This permission is optional and can also be managed through the device settings. The app may also request permission to send notifications. Allowing notifications makes it possible for the app to display alerts as supported notifications become available. Notification permissions can be changed later through the iPhone settings. APP Face ID Allow Notifications View the Website Dashboard After logging in, the Home screen provides a quick snapshot of the selected Brilliant Directories website. The dashboard includes: Members Snapshot: View the total number of members along with activity for today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days. Revenue: See total revenue along with revenue totals for today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days. Website Snapshot: Confirm the website name, domain, Site ID, country, and current website status. This screen is useful for quickly checking the overall status of a website without opening individual reports. Switch Between Brilliant Directories Websites Admins who manage more than one Brilliant Directories website can switch between sites directly from the app. Tap the website selector near the top of the screen to open the website list. The search field can be used to locate a specific website, while the star icon identifies a favorite website for easier access. Each website is displayed with its website name and Site ID, helping distinguish between multiple sites with similar names. View Members The Members tab provides quick access to member accounts associated with the selected website. Each member entry displays basic information such as the member name, listing type, and account status. Tap the + icon to expand the member record and view additional information. Expanded member details can include: Email address Phone number Address Revenue associated with the member Tap the − icon to collapse the member details again. A search field at the top of the screen can be used to filter the displayed member records when working with larger databases. Monitor Revenue The Revenue tab provides a mobile view of transactions associated with the website. Each entry can display the transaction amount, payment status, and the membership plan or product connected with the payment. For example, an entry may show a $100 Paid transaction for a particular membership plan or a smaller payment associated with a one-time purchase. Tap the + icon beside a transaction to view additional information when available. Filter Revenue Records The revenue search tools make it easier to locate a specific payment when multiple transactions are available. Revenue records can be filtered using options such as: User Email User Name Product Name For example, selecting User Email and entering a member's email address can quickly narrow the transaction list to payments associated with that member. Review Inbox Form Submissions The Inbox tab provides access to website form submissions received through supported forms. Each inbox entry identifies the form that generated the submission along with basic information such as the submitter's email address and submission date. Tap the + icon to expand a submission and review the information submitted through the form. Depending on the form, this can include fields such as: Name Email Phone Number Message For example, a submission from the website's Contact Us form can be expanded to view the visitor's contact information and message directly from the app. Review Website Activity The Activity tab provides a chronological view of activity recorded for the selected website. Entries are organized by date and activity type, including categories such as System , Admin Accounts , and Admin Action . Tap the + icon beside an activity entry to expand it and review additional details when available. This provides a quick way to check recent administrative or system activity while away from the full Admin Dashboard. Search and Filter Information Several sections of the app include a Filter search field that can be used to narrow the records currently displayed. This is especially useful when a website contains a large number of members, transactions, form submissions, or activity records. Instead of scrolling through the complete list, enter identifying information to locate the relevant entry more quickly. The bottom of applicable screens also displays how many records are currently loaded compared with the total number of available entries. Access Account Options Tap the profile icon in the upper-left corner of the app to open the account menu. From this menu, admins can access: Privacy Policy Terms and Conditions Log Out Current app version information The email address associated with the logged-in admin account is also displayed in this menu. When to Use the BD App vs. the Full Admin Dashboard The Brilliant Directories app is useful when an admin needs quick access to important website information without opening the full Admin Dashboard. For example, an admin could use the app to check whether a new member has joined, confirm recent revenue, review a Contact Us submission, or see recent website activity while away from a computer. For more extensive website configuration, content management, design changes, billing administration, or other advanced management tasks, the full Brilliant Directories Admin Dashboard remains the primary workspace. results.title: Authorize.net Payment Gateway - Frequently Asked Questions | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Authorize.net Payment Gateway - Frequently Asked Questions Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109695 1. If I update my Authorize.Net payment gateway to a new Authorize.Net account in BD, then for existing recurring members whose payment information is currently stored within Brilliant Directories, would BD continue to have access to the existing stored payment credentials after I configure the new Authorize.Net gateway? Yes. The cards are stored encrypted in your site's billing system. Saving new Authorize.Net credentials only updates the gateway's own settings (the Login ID and Transaction Key). It does not change any member's stored card or any member's subscription. 2. When an existing member's next recurring invoice becomes due, would BD submit that member's existing stored payment information through the new Authorize.Net gateway, without requiring the member to re-enter their card information? Yes. Each renewal is charged by sending the member's stored card to whichever Authorize.Net credentials are configured at the time the invoice is charged. Once the new credentials are saved, renewals go to the new account with nothing required from members. 3. If the existing stored payment information remains valid, would recurring billing therefore continue normally through the new gateway? It should, as long as the new Authorize.Net account accepts the charges. That depends on the new account's own settings, which we can't see from our side, so before switching we recommend confirming these three things in the new account: It accepts charges submitted without a card security code (CVV). Security codes are never stored, so renewals are always sent without one. If the new account declines transactions that have no security code, renewals would be declined. Its address verification (AVS) filter won't decline renewal charges. On your current account, every renewal comes back with address verification marked as not applicable, so address checks have not been applied to your renewals so far. Every card brand your members use is enabled. This includes American Express, which about a third of your members with a stored card use, and which some merchant accounts require enabling separately. If one of these settings did cause declines, the fix would be adjusting that setting in the new Authorize.Net account. Members would not need to re-enter their cards. 4. Under what circumstances, if any, would an existing recurring member be required to re-enter or update their payment information solely because the Authorize.Net gateway account was changed? For members with a stored card, none. Changing the account does not remove or invalidate their stored cards. 5. Please distinguish this from an underlying processor change on the same Authorize.Net gateway. My question specifically concerns replacing the existing Authorize.Net gateway account in BD with an entirely new Authorize.Net gateway account and new gateway credentials. A processor change behind your existing Authorize.Net account keeps the same Login ID and Transaction Key, so nothing changes on the Brilliant Directories side and billing continues as it does today. Replacing the account with a new Authorize.Net account and new credentials is the scenario covered above: stored cards stay in your site's billing system, and renewals start going to the new account. On the ARB point: Brilliant Directories does not use Authorize.Net's recurring billing (ARB) subscriptions. Your site keeps its own renewal schedule and sends each renewal to Authorize.Net as an individual charge, so the ARB data that can't be migrated is not something your site relies on. If you do decide to switch, it's done by editing the existing Authorize.net entry under Finance > Payment Settings in your admin and replacing the Login ID and Transaction Key. results.title: Settings » Domain Manager » DNS Records | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Settings » Domain Manager » DNS Records Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109758 The DNS tab in Settings > Domain Manager shows the records used by the website domain. Depending on where DNS is hosted, this tab is either an editor for the connected zone or a read-only view of public records. Identify which mode is available DNS arrangement Available behavior Connected Cloudflare account and matching domain Read and edit records in the connected Cloudflare zone, including supported proxy controls. Brilliant Directories nameservers and an available hosted zone Read and edit the domain's BD-hosted DNS records. Third-party DNS with the domain pointed at the BD site Inspect public records. Make changes at the external DNS provider. The tab may be absent when the website still uses a free platform address or the domain has no supported connection to inspect. Check Domain first. On a website whose address is a subdomain, such as members.example.com , the tab shows the parent domain's zone ( example.com ). If the subdomain has been given its own separate DNS zone, its records are not listed here; manage them at the DNS provider for that zone. Search and inspect editable records Open Settings > Domain Manager > DNS . Review All DNS records . Use the search box to find a name or value. Filter by record type when needed. If a required record is not listed, click the Show all button below the list (for example, Show all 31 records ). The default view lists the most relevant records first; a search or type filter always includes every matching record. Refresh reloads the record list. Copy controls help transfer an exact value without retyping it. Records can also be sorted by their name or type. Brilliant Directories DNS example: selfautomated.com A BD-hosted DNS zone filtered to CNAME records. Use the record filter and search to locate the required entry. Cloudflare DNS example: demotailwind.com This is a separate domain using the Cloudflare editor. It illustrates the alternative DNS arrangement, rather than the next step for selfautomated.com. On a Cloudflare-connected site, the DNS tab also shows the Cloudflare connection, Point your domain with a different DNS host , and Email delivery records above the record list. The connected Cloudflare DNS editor exposes the proxy controls. Website records are proxied in this example; sender-authentication records remain Direct. Add or change a record Confirm that the displayed zone is the intended domain. Choose the add-record action, or the edit action on the existing record. Select the required record type: A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, or MX. Enter the name and value supplied by the service being configured. For supported Cloudflare address records, choose Through Cloudflare or Direct as appropriate. Save the record. Refresh the list and confirm the saved values. The add-record form shown here returns to the selfautomated.com example with Brilliant Directories DNS. Expand Add a record to enter the values supplied by the service being configured. For MX changes that require a specific priority, use the authoritative DNS provider’s full DNS editor. The basic record form does not expose a separate priority field. To move incoming email to a different provider, follow the checks in Mailboxes and Email Routing . Website pointing records should use the site-specific instructions in the connection guide . Email-authentication records should use the values generated in Emails > Sender Authentication . Avoid generic examples for either task. Changes affect the live domain. Editing or deleting a record can interrupt the website, email, or another service. Keep the original values and remove only the intended record. Do not proxy mail-service or sender-authentication records that need Direct / DNS only access. Inspect public records at another provider Open Public DNS records . Click Check again . Review the record's purpose, value, and Seen by result. Make any required correction at the DNS provider. Return to the tab and recheck after the provider publishes the change. The public view compares answers from Google and Cloudflare resolvers for the records it checks, including nameservers, web addresses, mail servers, SPF, other TXT records, DKIM, DMARC, and DNSSEC delegation records. Google + Cloudflare indicates agreement; Needs attention can indicate a missing record or differing answers. This view does not enumerate every possible hostname or grant editing access to the provider's zone. Success means the intended value is saved in the authoritative DNS editor and the public checks reflect the required configuration. Public resolvers can temporarily disagree while cached answers expire. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Settings » Domain Manager » Cloudflare Connection and Settings | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Settings » Domain Manager » Cloudflare Connection and Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109759 The Cloudflare tab connects a Cloudflare-managed domain to Domain Manager. A connected account can support website pointing, DNS record management, email-authentication publication, and Cloudflare settings from the BD admin area. Before starting Use a custom domain that exists in an accessible Cloudflare account. Have permission to authorize that account and domain. Keep a record of the current DNS and email settings. Use Sign in with Cloudflare to authorize your account and connect your domain to Domain Manager. For a free directoryup.com address, use the domain connection wizard to authorize Cloudflare and choose a custom domain. For creating the Cloudflare zone and moving nameservers, see Connecting a Site to Cloudflare . Authorizing Domain Manager is separate from registering a domain or changing its nameservers. Connect a domain while changing the website address Open the domain connection wizard. Select Use a domain from my Cloudflare account . Sign in and authorize the intended account. Filter the domain list and select the intended domain. Choose the main address or enter the required subdomain. Click Use this address to prepare its DNS records. Review Switch Over , then complete its separate confirmation. A domain whose main address is already in use can still offer an available subdomain. Selecting the main address also points the root domain; selecting a subdomain leaves other addresses on that domain unchanged. The Cloudflare connection wizard offers the main domain or a subdomain after authorization. Alternative: connect an account for the current domain Use these steps when the website already has its domain and Cloudflare still needs to be connected. If the wizard above already connected the account, continue to the next section. Open Settings > Domain Manager > Cloudflare . Click Sign in with Cloudflare . Sign in to the appropriate Cloudflare account. Review and authorize the requested access. Return to Domain Manager. Confirm that Connected to Cloudflare shows the intended domain. If sign-in cannot find the domain or authorization is unavailable, check the account and domain access before making changes. Do not continue using a connection associated with a different domain. A connection made earlier with a Cloudflare API token shows An API token under Signed in using , with a Switch to signing in with Cloudflare link. New connections use Cloudflare sign-in only. A successful authorization identifies demotailwind.com as the connected Cloudflare domain. Point the website and publish email records Review the connected domain and the website's displayed target. Use Point my domain at my website when that action is needed. Review the resulting connection status. Under Email delivery records , use Add my email records to Cloudflare when offered. Open Emails and recheck sender authentication. For changing the website to a different domain, follow the separate connection wizard . Pointing records and switching the website's primary address are distinct actions. Manage DNS records Use the DNS tab to inspect, add, edit, or delete supported records. Through Cloudflare sends supported website traffic through the Cloudflare proxy. Direct exposes the underlying DNS destination. Email-related records must use the mode required by the mail provider; sender-authentication CNAME records should remain Direct. See DNS Records . Review Cloudflare settings Set recommended defaults applies the Domain Manager's recommended configuration. Review the current settings and the confirmation before applying it, especially when the domain already has a custom configuration. Always use https controls redirection to HTTPS. Security level & bot fighting controls the available security level. Minimum encryption version sets the lowest accepted TLS version. The recommended defaults enable Always use https and insecure-image HTTPS rewrites, select Full encryption, set minimum TLS to 1.2 and security to Medium, enable HTTP/3, faster repeat visits, Brotli, Early Hints, and Smart Tiered Cache, and turn off Hotlink protection. Bot Fight Mode is not changed by this action. Check the result for any setting the Cloudflare account does not allow to be updated. The Settings card with the recommended values shown: Always use https on, security level Medium, and minimum TLS 1.2. Set recommended defaults applies them in one step. Page caching Find Page caching . Review the displayed caching behavior. Set the offered cache lifetime within the supported 30–3600 second range. Click Turn on page caching . Review the saved status. Use Clear cached pages when cached pages need to be refreshed. Check important public and signed-in workflows after changing caching behavior. Page caching has its own lifetime and activation controls. This example shows caching turned off. Advanced settings Click Show beside Advanced settings to inspect HTTP/3, faster repeat visits, compression, Early Hints, Smart Tiered Cache, encryption mode, insecure-image handling, Bot Fight Mode, and hotlink protection. Availability and allowed changes can depend on the Cloudflare account and the current site configuration. Full (strict) requires a trusted certificate for the website hostname on the origin server. Review SSL > Certificate on your server before changing encryption mode. If the panel refuses an unsafe change, resolve the stated prerequisite instead of forcing the setting at another screen. Show expands the advanced settings. Encryption mode, marked, is the one setting here that can take the website offline if it is wrong; Full is recommended. Unavailable controls depend on the Cloudflare connection. Disconnect Disconnect stops Domain Manager from managing Cloudflare. Existing DNS records remain in place, and existing Cloudflare settings and proxying continue until separately changed. Reconnect the account to resume management from Domain Manager. The wizard can publish website sender-authentication records without creating incoming mailboxes or their MX records. Review Mailboxes separately if the domain will receive email. A completed setup shows the correct connected domain, the expected website connection, and verified email-authentication records. Test the website and email after applying any settings. results.title: Settings » Domain Manager » Mailboxes and Email Routing | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Settings » Domain Manager » Mailboxes and Email Routing Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109760 The Mailboxes tab in Settings > Domain Manager identifies where incoming email is delivered and provides the available mailbox controls. It is separate from the outgoing sender-authentication checks in Emails . Before starting Use a custom domain and confirm which provider should receive its email. The visible actions depend on the domain's DNS connection and whether local mailboxes are supported. Moving mail to another provider requires that provider's account, mailbox setup, and exact records. Back up messages before removing mailboxes or changing a mail-hosting arrangement. Check the current mail provider Open Settings > Domain Manager > Mailboxes . Read Who handles your email . Review the provider and routing result before changing any mailbox. MX records decide where new incoming mail goes. A locally listed mailbox does not prove that the domain currently delivers new mail to it. If the domain uses Google, Microsoft, Cloudflare Email Routing, or another provider, manage the active inboxes at that provider unless a deliberate migration is being performed. The example uses selfautomated.com with Brilliant Directories-hosted mail throughout. Who handles your email (1) reports where new mail for the domain is delivered. Add and manage a local mailbox Find Mailboxes . Click Add a mailbox when offered. Enter the requested mailbox details and password. Set the storage limit. Save the mailbox. Click Refresh and confirm it appears. Each mailbox displays space used and its limit, with Open webmail , Set up , and More buttons. Open webmail is described under Open a mailbox in webmail . Set up shows the connection settings and can email them with Email these instructions to . More holds Change the password , Change the storage limit , and Delete this mailbox . A limit of 0 means no individual mailbox limit; the website's hosting capacity still applies. Use Set up for the exact connection settings for Outlook, Apple Mail, or a phone. Confirm the recipient before sending setup instructions. Set up (1) expands the connection settings (2) for the existing matt@selfautomated.com mailbox. It displays the exact connection settings without exposing the password. Deleting a mailbox also deletes its stored messages. Deletion requires confirmation of the full email address and cannot be undone from Domain Manager. Preserve any messages that must be kept first. Open a mailbox in webmail Open webmail opens the mailbox's inbox in a new browser window, already signed in, without the mailbox password. It works the same way as Check Email in cPanel. Find the mailbox under Mailboxes . Click Open webmail . Read and send mail in the new window. A mailbox row: the Catch-all label (1) marks the mailbox that receives mail sent to addresses that do not exist, and Open webmail (2) opens its inbox signed in. Signing in without the password is available to administrators whose role can open the website's cPanel. For other administrators, Open webmail opens the ordinary webmail sign-in page, which asks for the mailbox password. If the browser blocks the new window, a message asks to allow pop-ups for the page; allow them and click Open webmail again. If the mail server cannot sign in to the mailbox, the new window shows the webmail sign-in page instead, and a message explains that the mailbox password is needed there. Each signed-in opening is recorded in the website's notifications as Webmail opened for the mailbox. The sign-in itself is never placed in a link or the browser address. A mailbox marked Catch-all receives email sent to addresses at the domain that do not exist; see Handle unrouted email . When that mail is kept in the account's own mailbox, that mailbox is listed too, as The account's own mailbox with the Catch-all label. It has no address at the domain and no usage figures ( Not reported ). For administrators whose role can open cPanel it offers only Open webmail , because webmail is the only way to read that mail; for other administrators it has no buttons. Set the website's sending address Email from your website controls the domain-based sending address offered by this panel. Use an address that is monitored and can receive replies, then recheck the outgoing authentication in Emails . This card appears when the domain has mailboxes on Brilliant Directories servers; otherwise, set the sending address under Emails with Your "from" address . Also check Emails > Your mailboxes' signature (DKIM) . Its Fix it action provides the signature record for mail sent from hosted mailboxes; this is separate from the website’s sender-authentication setup. Handle unrouted email Send all unrouted email for the following domain controls messages addressed to names without an existing mailbox. Choose one of three options, then click Save : Bounce it back rejects these messages. This is the safer choice, because a sender who mistypes an address finds out. Keep in the catch-all mailbox holds them in the account's own mailbox, which is then listed under Mailboxes with Open webmail . Send it to delivers them to the address entered below it. When that address is one of the domain's own mailboxes, it is marked Catch-all in the mailbox list. When mail is currently kept in the account's own mailbox, the card says so ( Right now it is kept in the catch-all mailbox , followed by its name). If no option is selected, Save asks for a choice instead of saving. Confirm the destination before saving so mail is not collected in an unintended inbox. Send all unrouted email offers Bounce it back, Keep in the catch-all mailbox, and Send it to (1); the note below explains each choice (2). Here, mail to addresses that do not exist goes to matt@selfautomated.com. Change the incoming email provider Prepare the destination provider's account and mailboxes. Open the DNS tab and keep a copy of the domain's current MX, SPF (TXT), and autodiscover records. Open Change your email provider . Click Change . Select Our mail servers , Google Workspace , Microsoft 365 , or Somewhere else . Enter or review the required provider values. Click Point my email here . Read the confirmation before approving the MX change. Refresh the provider result. Open the DNS tab and confirm the result: only the new provider's MX records remain, and the SPF and autodiscover records are still present. Remove any MX record left from the previous provider, and restore any missing record from the copy. Test incoming email at the destination. Check the DNS records after every provider change. The automated change can leave an MX record from the previous provider in place or remove the domain's SPF or autodiscover record. A leftover MX record can keep sending some incoming mail to the old provider, and a missing SPF record can send the website's email to spam. Compare the records with the copy taken before the change. After Change is clicked, Change your email provider offers four choices (1): Our mail servers , Google Workspace , Microsoft 365 , and Somewhere else . Cancel closes it without changes. The automated action replaces the existing MX records where the panel has the required DNS access. For externally hosted DNS without that access, update the records at the DNS provider. Use the destination provider's exact hostname rather than a generic example. This changes delivery routing; it does not migrate stored messages or create a paid account at the destination provider. If the panel identifies a mismatch between local mail delivery and server routing, it may offer Deliver my mail here . Use that only when the local server is the intended mail destination. The reverse case, where the domain's mail goes to another provider but this server still keeps mail for the domain, shows This server still delivers your mail to itself with a Send my mail to button for that provider. If an old Brilliant Directories MX record outranks the provider's records, the panel removes it where it manages the DNS, or explains how to remove it at the DNS provider. Completion means new mail reaches the intended provider, outgoing website mail passes authentication, and mailbox applications can connect with the displayed settings. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: Settings » Domain Manager » Diagnostics | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Settings » Domain Manager » Diagnostics Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109761 The Diagnostics tab in Settings > Domain Manager runs additional website checks and shows relevant certificate and update details. It helps identify the next action when a general status message is not enough to explain a problem. Before starting The administrator must have permission to view website resources. Review the Domain and SSL findings first so an address or certificate problem is not confused with a pending software update. Run the checks Open Settings > Domain Manager > Diagnostics . Find Is anything on this website broken? . Click Check everything . Wait for the results. Expand the relevant details for any reported finding. The checks cover website launch status, purchased items awaiting installation, certificate problems, and pending updates. A result describes the checks available to this tool; it is not a full audit of every custom page or integration. Review certificate attempts Certificate attempt history appears when relevant records are available. Review the latest result and expand the detail when needed. Repeated earlier attempts can help explain what happened, while the current SSL result shows the website's present certificate state. Use an offered repair Depending on the finding, the page may offer Fix these for me or Run the certificate self-heal . Read the explanation and confirmation before applying the action. Re-run the checks afterward and verify the public website. Review pending updates Find Updates waiting for your website . Click Check for updates . Review the listed updates. Choose the specific update or Install all when that is intended. Read and confirm the installation prompt. Recheck after installation completes. Installation applies changes to the website. The confirmation identifies changes that cannot be undone from this screen. Review the update list before proceeding. If a repair fails or the public website remains affected, contact support with the site ID, domain, exact result, and the action already attempted. Avoid repeatedly running a repair without reviewing its latest result. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . results.title: Settings » Domain Manager » Speed Tests | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Settings » Domain Manager » Speed Tests Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109762 The Speed tab in Settings > Domain Manager runs Google PageSpeed Insights tests for the website homepage and keeps previous results for comparison. Before starting The website must have a successfully detected HTTPS certificate, and the administrator must have permission to view website resources. If the tab is missing, check SSL and the administrator's access permissions first. Run a performance test Open Settings > Domain Manager > Speed . Find PageSpeed Insights . Click Run the test . Keep the page open while the mobile and desktop tests complete. Review both sets of results. A run normally takes around half a minute, but the testing service can take longer. The panel allows one combined mobile-and-desktop run every 24 hours per website. If a recent result is already available, use it and the saved history instead of repeatedly starting another run. Read the results Compare the mobile and desktop scores separately. Review the metrics, flagged issues, and suggested improvements below the scores. Scores describe the test conditions at that time; they are not a guarantee of every visitor's experience or a promised search ranking. Alongside performance, the results show Google's Accessibility , Best practices , SEO , and Agentic browsing scores. Use the history to compare measurements after a website change. If a test fails, confirm that the homepage loads over HTTPS and review the error before retrying when permitted. Example test results. A comparison graph becomes available after a second saved test. Improve and measure again Start with the specific large files, loading delays, or other issues identified in the result. Retest after the change when the next test is available. See bandwidth optimization for related advice on resource use. The Speed tab uses Google PageSpeed Insights to test the website’s performance and track results over time. If you need help investigating an issue, the Brilliant Directories support team may use additional diagnostic tools to take a closer look. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: Account Dashboard » Update Profile | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Account Dashboard » Update Profile Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109946 The Update Profile page in the Account Dashboard holds the contact details of the signed-in admin account: profile photo, name, job title, company, contact email and phone number, additional email addresses and phone numbers, email signature, and website and social profile links. The Brilliant Directories support and billing teams use these details to know who they are talking to and where to send replies. The page edits only the account that is signed in. Other admins on a website update their own profiles from their own accounts. Before Starting Sign in to the Account Dashboard . The Sign-in email cannot be changed from this page. Contact support to change it. How to Open Update Profile In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right. Select Update Profile . Update Profile is also listed in the Account menu on the left of every account page, together with Notification Settings, Login Settings, Verified Users and Change Password. Profile Settings Profile photo – Click Upload photo and choose a JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP image up to 5MB. The image is cropped to a square and saved as soon as it uploads. Once a photo is set, Change photo replaces it and Remove deletes it. Full name – Required. The name of the person who uses this admin account. Job title – Optional. Company – Optional. Sign-in email – The email address used to sign in. It is shown for reference only ( Contact support to change ). Email address – The address where Brilliant Directories should reach the admin. The star button next to an email address marks it as the primary email address for billing & support replies . The line under the field shows which address is currently the primary one. Phone number – The main contact phone number, marked with a star as the primary phone. Additional emails & phone numbers – Click to expand. The list loads from the account's support records. Click Add another address or Add another number to add one, click the star next to an entry to make it the primary one, or remove an entry with its remove button. Email signature – Click to expand. The signature is appended to emails sent from the account. Use the editor toolbar for formatting; text colour, size and alignment are not kept. Website & social profiles – Click to expand. Enter full addresses starting with http:// or https:// . Save Changes – Saves every field except the photo, which saves on upload. After Saving The message Your profile has been saved. appears once the changes are stored. When a different address is chosen as the primary email, the line under Email address adds pending review . The Brilliant Directories team reviews profile changes before applying them to the account's support records, so the new primary email, additional emails and photo reach support records after that review. results.title: Account Dashboard » Login Settings | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Account Dashboard » Login Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109947 The Login Settings page in the Account Dashboard controls how the signed-in admin account signs in: two-factor authentication, the available sign-in methods, and the ManageMyDirectory.com mobile app for notifications on a phone. Before Starting Sign in to the Account Dashboard . Turning on two-factor authentication requires access to the inbox of the account's sign-in email, since the one-time codes are sent there. How to Open Login Settings In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right. Select Login Settings . Login Settings is also listed in the Account menu on the left of every account page. Login Settings Sections Two-Factor Authentication – Shows whether two-factor sign-in is On or Off . With two-factor on, a one-time code is emailed to the sign-in email whenever the account signs in from a new device, so a password alone is not enough to sign in. Sign-in Methods – Lists the ways this account can sign in. Email and password shows the sign-in email and an Active badge. Google and Apple are marked Coming soon and are not available yet. Get Notifications on Your App – The App Store and Google Play buttons open the ManageMyDirectory.com mobile app. After the app is installed and signed in once, the devices that are signed in and receiving notifications are listed here with the time each was last seen. Notification Settings opens the page that controls which notifications are sent. Turn On Two-Factor Authentication In the Two-Factor Authentication section, click Turn on two-factor . A one-time code is emailed to the account's sign-in email right away. Under Enter your code , type the code from the email. Click Verify & turn on . If the email does not arrive, click Resend code . The code expires shortly, so use the most recent one. When the code is accepted, the confirmation Two-factor is on appears and the section shows the On badge. From then on, signing in from a new device asks for a one-time code sent by email. For more about how two-factor sign-in works, see Enhancing Security with Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) . results.title: Account Dashboard » Verified Users | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Account Dashboard » Verified Users Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109948 The Verified Users page in the Account Dashboard lists the people the Brilliant Directories support and billing teams may contact about the account's websites, and what each person can discuss. A website owner can give a colleague, partner or assistant access here directly, instead of asking support to add them. Each verified user gets one of three access levels: Billing & Support – Can be contacted about both billing and support matters. Billing Only – Can be contacted about billing matters only. Support Only – Can be contacted about support matters only. Before Starting Sign in to the Account Dashboard with the account that owns the websites. The page is for website owners: an account that does not own any active, suspended or pending website sees a message explaining there is nothing to set. Verified users are stored in the account's support records. If the page shows We could not reach your support record just now , saving may not work until the record is available again; try later or contact support. Verified users are contacts for support and billing. Adding someone here does not give them a login to the website admin. To add an admin login, see Settings » Admin Accounts . How to Open Verified Users In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right. Select Update Profile (or any other account page). In the Account menu on the left, click Verified Users . Add a Verified User Email address – Enter the person's email address. It can be an email already on the account or a new one for someone else. Access level – Choose Billing & Support , Billing Only or Support Only . Websites – Click to choose which websites this person is a contact for. Search by name, URL or ID, tick the websites, then click Done . Select all shown and Clear tick or untick the whole list. Remove – The trash button removes the person from the list. All my websites – Makes the person a contact for every website on the account, including any website added later. Add another email – Adds a row for another person. Save changes – Saves the list. Adding, changing or removing a person takes effect only after saving. Every person needs at least one website, or All my websites . A person with no websites is not saved, and a message names them. After Saving The message Verified users were saved. confirms the change. The support and billing teams then use this list to confirm who may be contacted about each website, and at which access level. Contacts that the Brilliant Directories team entered earlier appear under On file with our support team . They cannot be changed on this page, but they show the full list of people on file. Contact support to change one of them. results.title: Account Dashboard » Change Password | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Account Dashboard » Change Password Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109949 The Change Password page in the Account Dashboard sets a new password for the signed-in admin account. Changing the password here also signs the account out of every session, on every browser and device, so anyone still signed in with the old password loses access. Before Starting Sign in to the Account Dashboard . The current password is required. If it is not known, use the forgot password link on the admin sign-in page instead. Have the new password ready before continuing: the current browser is signed out as soon as the password changes. How to Open Change Password In the Account Dashboard, click the admin name at the top right. Select Login Settings (or any other account page). In the Account menu on the left, click Change Password . Change the Password Enter the Current password . Enter the New password . Check the requirements under the field. Each one is marked as it is met: At least 10 characters A letter and a number, or 16+ characters Different from your current password Both new password fields match Enter the same password again in Confirm new password . Click Change password . The button becomes available once every requirement is met. The new password is also refused if it is one of the most commonly guessed passwords, matches the admin's name or email address, was used before on this account, is longer than 72 characters, or starts or ends with a space. The page shows a message explaining which rule was not met. After the Password Changes The message Your password has been changed. Signing you out so you can sign in with it. appears, and the sign-in page opens with Please sign in with your new password. Every session for the account is signed out, including the current one. Other browsers and devices must sign in again with the new password. Any reset your password links sent to the account earlier stop working. A confirmation email is sent to the account's sign-in email, so an unexpected change is noticed straight away. Too many incorrect attempts. After several incorrect current passwords, the page stops accepting attempts for 15 minutes. Wait, then try again, or use the forgot password link on the sign-in page. results.title: How to Capture a HAR File and Console Screenshot for Support | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: How to Capture a HAR File and Console Screenshot for Support Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109959 Some problems only happen on one computer or in one browser: a button that does nothing when clicked, a save that seems to work but does not keep the changes, a form that will not submit, or a page that keeps loading. When the support team cannot make the problem happen on its own computers, a recording from the browser where it does happen shows exactly what went wrong. This article explains how to make that recording and send it to support. It takes about five minutes and does not change anything on the website. What Support Needs The browser name and version , EG Chrome 154 on Windows 11. See How to Find the Browser Version at the end of this article. A HAR file. This is a log of everything the browser sent and received while the problem happened. The file name ends in .har . A screenshot of the Console tab , taken right after the problem happens. Error messages from the page show up here in red. A list of active browser extensions or assistant tools , EG Grammarly, ad blockers, password managers, translation tools, or AI assistants and sidebars. These tools can change how a page behaves. The page address and the steps that cause the problem , EG "Settings > General Settings, change the Website Name, click Save Changes". Keep the HAR file private. A HAR file can contain anything typed into forms on the page, and in some browsers the admin login session. Attach it only to the support ticket, never to a public post or a group email. Sign out of the Admin Area after sending it, which ends the login session recorded in the file. Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge Chrome and Edge use the same developer tools, so the steps are the same. Button names can differ slightly between versions. Open the page where the problem happens. Press F12 (on a Mac, Option + Command + I ), or right-click anywhere on the page and choose Inspect . The developer tools open on one side of the window. Click the Network tab. If it is not visible, click the » arrows next to the tab names to find it. Tick Keep log so the list is not cleared when the page reloads or moves to another page. Older versions of Chrome call this option Preserve log . Repeat the steps that cause the problem, EG click the button or submit the form. New lines appear in the list while the browser works. Wait until the problem has happened. Click the Export HAR button (the downward arrow in the Network toolbar), choose where to save the file, and click Save . Click the Console tab and take a screenshot of it, including any lines shown in red. On Windows, press Windows + Shift + S . On a Mac, press Command + Shift + 4 . Sanitized HAR files: Chrome saves a sanitized HAR file by default. It leaves out the browser's login cookies but keeps everything support needs to investigate. If a menu appears with two choices, choose Export HAR (sanitized) . In older versions of Chrome, the same file can also be saved by right-clicking the list of requests and choosing Save all as HAR with content . Mozilla Firefox Open the page where the problem happens. Press F12 (on a Mac, Option + Command + I ), or right-click anywhere on the page and choose Inspect . Click the Network tab. Click the gear icon at the right end of the Network toolbar and select Persist Logs , so a check mark appears next to it. Repeat the steps that cause the problem and wait until it has happened. Click the gear icon again and choose Save All As HAR , then save the file. The same option appears when right-clicking the list of requests. Click the Console tab and take a screenshot of it. Firefox has no sanitized option, so its HAR files include the login cookies. Signing out of the Admin Area after sending the file ends that session. Safari (Mac) Safari hides its developer tools until they are turned on. This only needs to be done once. Choose Safari > Settings , click Advanced , and tick Show features for web developers . A Develop menu appears in the menu bar. Open the page where the problem happens, then choose Develop > Show Web Inspector (or press Option + Command + I ). Click the Network tab. Click the round filter icon next to All and choose Preserve Requests , so the list is not cleared when the page reloads. Repeat the steps that cause the problem and wait until it has happened. Click Export at the right end of the Network toolbar and save the file. Click the Console tab and take a screenshot of it. How to Send the Files Attach the .har file and the Console screenshot to the support ticket, either by replying to the ticket email or through the support portal. If the HAR file is too large to attach, compress it into a .zip file first. In the same reply, include the browser name and version, the list of active extensions or assistant tools, the page address, and the steps that cause the problem. Sign out of the Admin Area, then sign back in. How to Find the Browser Version Chrome: open the three-dot menu and choose Help > About Google Chrome . Edge: open the three-dot menu and choose Help and feedback > About Microsoft Edge . Firefox: open the menu (three lines) and choose Help > About Firefox . Safari: choose Safari > About Safari . For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.title: 10/02/2026 - Software Updates | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: 10/02/2026 - Software Updates Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000109975 We made updates to several default widgets this week. If you customized any of these widgets and want to update them, you can find the latest code in the corresponding default widget. Please remember that if you have a custom version of any of these widgets, the latest updates will not be pushed to your website. Released a new Account area in the Admin where each Admin can manage their own login. Profile details such as name, phone, company, timezone, photo, email signature and social links can now be edited there, the password can be changed from the same place, and notifications can now be set per delivery channel - website, desktop and mobile - either for all websites at once or website by website. In addition, a website owner can now grant another email address Billing and Support access to their websites from the same area. Along with this, the handling of Admin login sessions was hardened. Improved the Google Maps alert in the Admin so it now reports the exact problem Google returned, such as billing not being enabled, a restricted referrer or an API that was never turned on, instead of one generic message for every case. Both the website key and the server-side key used for member geocoding are now checked, and the key is also tested on the website's own domain so the result reflects what visitors actually see. In addition, the website key, the server key and the New Google Maps Places API switch can now be edited and validated from inside the alert, and a key Google rejects is not saved. Improved the domain connection wizard in the Domain Manager in the Admin so connecting a root domain now shows the recommended instructions for that domain's DNS provider: domain forwarding for GoDaddy and an ALIAS record for Namecheap, with the A record kept only as the fallback for other providers. Improved the SSL tab of the Domain Manager in the Admin. The SSL tab now shows the date a managed certificate renews instead of only stating that it renews on its own, an SPF record that repeats the same entry is now reported as a problem instead of being accepted as correct, and the Point Domain step now names the service that actually hosts the domain's DNS rather than always naming the registrar. Fixed three issues in the Domain Manage r in the Admin : the notice explaining that the www prefix had been removed from the typed domain was never visible, the summary reported that everything looked good while the Emails tab showed rows that needed attention, and three messages pointed to an Emails screen that does not exist. Added the Member Credit balance as a selectable field when exporting members from the Admin. Added live validation to the Additional CSS field under Design Settings in the Admin . Errors such as a missing closing brace are now highlighted while the CSS is being edited, before they can affect how the website renders. Updated the code editor fields used across the Admin , including in the Design Settings , the page and email template editors, the robots.txt editor and the Post Types field editor, to a newer version. Added an optional cancellation reason when ending a member's subscription in the Admin. The reason is now stored together with the cancellation, and it can also be entered when cancelling from the Transactions page. Improved the speed of member search results on websites with large member databases by removing an unnecessary duplicate-removal step from the search query whenever the search cannot return duplicate members. Widget Involved: Search - Member - Search Query Started a UI design update for the Admin, starting with a new side menu and header and a rebuilt 301 Redirect Rules page in the Developer Hub. Admin pages that have not been converted yet keep their current appearance. Fixed an issue that caused the image options popup in the Froala Editor to open about one screen below the clicked image when a member edited an article in the Member Dashboard , which put the Alternate Text control out of reach until the page was scrolled. Widget Involved: Form - Froala Editor Javascript Fixed an issue that prevented some images from loading on websites using an image CDN. Fixed an issue that prevented support tickets from being listed in the Admin when the Admin's login email contained a plus sign. Fixed an issue that caused a request for a single record on the API to report the totals and paging of the whole table, which made integrations read the response as a list instead of one record. Fixed an issue that caused the member category CSV import in the Admin to silently drop a sub-category whose name was exactly two characters long and move its sub-sub-category up to take its place. Fixed an issue that prevented a saved automatic sitemap update schedule from being installed on some websites, so the sitemap stopped rebuilding on the chosen frequency and the tool reported automatic updates as turned off. Fixed an issue that caused the Login Date in Show Active Sessions in the Admin to be displayed in Pacific time instead of the website's own timezone. Fixed an issue that caused the structured data (schema) on public pages to report a last modified date of the first day of the current month on every page, and to claim a last reviewed date for a review that never took place. Pages now report the date the listing, post or page was actually last saved, and the last reviewed date was removed. Fixed an issue that caused a member or post title containing a double quote or angle brackets to break the links and image descriptions on search results and profile listings. results.title: Can I Send A Mass Email Campaign Using Brilliant Directories? | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Can I Send A Mass Email Campaign Using Brilliant Directories? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558357 The built-in email system is designed for emailing active members who have requested to receive emails from the site. A common example would be sending a monthly newsletter to members who have opted in to receive updates. The email system also sends transactional emails, such as new member signup notifications, credit card update notices, lead emails, and other system-generated messages related to member activity. Sending mass unsolicited emails to Claim Listings or an imported contact list may be considered spam. This can violate email compliance laws, damage the sending reputation of your domain, and result in future emails being blocked or blacklisted. In some cases, sending spam messages can also negatively impact other sites on the same server and may lead to account restrictions or termination with Brilliant Directories. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard . Was this article helpful and accurate? results.content: Emails » Email Accounts Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558363 Email accounts (mailboxes) at the website's own domain, such as support@example.com , are created and managed in Settings > Domain Manager > Mailboxes . The Emails > Email Accounts menu item opens that tab directly. Before starting Connect a custom domain to the website. A free directoryup.com address has no mailboxes of its own. Confirm which provider receives the domain's email. Mailboxes on the website's hosting receive new mail only when the domain's MX records point to them. Open the email accounts In the admin, open Emails . Click Email Accounts . Domain Manager opens on the Mailboxes tab, which lists the mailboxes, their storage use, and where the domain's email is delivered. Email Accounts in the Emails menu (1) opens Domain Manager on the Mailboxes tab (2). Create and manage mailboxes On the Mailboxes tab, Add a mailbox creates a new mailbox with its password and storage limit. Each mailbox in the list offers Open webmail , Set up for the settings to enter in Outlook, Apple Mail, or a phone, and More for changing the password or storage limit or deleting the mailbox. The full steps are in Settings » Domain Manager » Mailboxes and Email Routing . Generic addresses such as info@ are more often treated as spam by receiving mail systems. Addresses such as support@ , admin@ , or contact@ are usually a better choice. When the previous Email Accounts page appears The previous Manage Email Accounts page still opens in two cases: The website uses a free directoryup.com address. The page explains that a live domain name must be connected before email accounts can be set up, and offers Connect Live Domain . See How to Connect a Domain to a Brilliant Directories Website . The administrator's role does not include access to the Domain Manager's Mailboxes tab. On a free directoryup.com address, Email Accounts shows the previous page with Connect Live Domain (1). Additional notes Email replies do not have a separate reply-to address. Responses go to the address that sent the original message. To read a mailbox in the browser, see How To Access Webmail Through the Admin Area . results.title: Email Forwarders | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
results.content: Email Forwarders Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558373 Email Forwarders Not Supported IMPORTANT: The Email Forwarders functionality has been removed from our implementation of cPanel as of June, 2024. Due to the way this functionality works in cPanel, it caused several issues for users. Some of these issue included: Not all emails being forwarded properly based on the domain settings of the email sender and the receiver of the forwarded email Sendgrid blocking emails from being sent to accounts hosted in cPanel, preventing the Admins of sites from getting notification emails The domain reputation and reputation of the server being harmed when SPAM emails are forwarded through this system While email forwarders can no longer be added or modified, any existing email forwarders will remain in place. If an email forwarder needs to be removed from a site, please submit a ticket to our Support Team for assistance. Recommendations to Replace Email Forwarders The recommended alternative for using email forwarders is to use an email app that can send and receive emails from multiple email accounts in one place: Gmail Paid Google Workspace email accounts can connect to 3rd party email accounts to send and receive emails. For this, the MX record would need to be pointed to Google workspace, for more information: How To Change Email MX Records Thunderbird This is a free desktop email application from Mozilla, the makers of the FireFox browser. Thunderbird offers an app for Windows, MacOS, and Linux operating systems. Apple Mail Apple includes a free email client that can connect to 3rd party email accounts for all of their devices and operating systems. Microsoft Windows Mail and Microsoft Outlook - Microsoft includes the Windows Mail and Outlook for Windows applications for free on devices using Windows 10 or newer. Both of these applications can connect to 3rd party email accounts. For additional assistance: Email support@brilliantdirectories.com or create a ticket Inside Your Account Dashboard .
